### What Do I Stand For?

It seems I was the only Democratic candidate to answer the [_Cardinal News_ survey](https://cardinalnews.org/how-to-vote-in-louisa-county/#/us-house-5th-district-democratic/5th-district-democrats/topic/biggest-challenge-us), which is a shame, because I put some thought into this and gave some interesting and fairly in-depth responses. So I’ll reproduce the survey and my answers here, so you can see where I stand—and also that I have a wider and more substantive set of policy positions than any other candidate in this race, of either party.
**What's the biggest challenge facing your district (or in the case of Senate candidate, the state) and how would you propose to address it?**
We have two big challenges, representing the character of this district, which is home to a world-class university, UVA, but also a heavily agricultural district. Both of those are being hit.

UVA has been struggling to maintain its academic independence, and it is an important center for scientific research, which has suffered from Trump's vandalism of science funding. At the same time, farmers in the rural parts of the district are getting hit hard by rising fuel and fertilizer prices, and Trump's trade war has restricted global markets for their crops.
Both of these are just a part of our big national crisis. Our district faces these challenges because the president has asserted unchecked power to declare war, impose tariffs, and make arbitrary decisions about spending. These are things that are supposed to be under the control of Congress, but our current Congress isn't doing its job and isn't standing up for their constituents.
**How would you assess the impact of HR 1, aka the One Big Beautiful Bill?**
HR 1 is a perfect example of how this Congress just acts as a rubber stamp for Donald Trump. It cut funding for all sorts of programs that benefit ordinary people in this district, from health care funding to food assistance, but it still did nothing to cut federal spending because it directed billions of dollars for ICE to send masked goons into our communities and ask people for their papers and to build massive detention centers where people with no criminal records are being held in notoriously inhumane conditions.

That is typical of this administration and its enablers in Congress. There's always money for programs designed to hurt people and never money for programs designed to help.
**What are your views on how Americans can better afford health care? Would you support the so-called "Medicare for All"? Why or why not?**
As a former Tea Party guy, I am very aware that Republicans have been promising for 16 years to "repeal and replace" Obamacare and propose something better, and somehow they never get around to it.

I support restoring the health care funding cut by HR1 to help put the system back together. And then I favor incremental reforms to lower costs and fix some of the perverse incentives built into the system as it is.

I don't support "Medicare for All," because I'm not convinced that will fix the actual problems. Even under Medicare as we have it now, we have dozens of rules that raise costs, limit access, and distort the system, and I favor incremental reforms to fix those problems.

Making heath care more affordable also requires standing up to the current anti-immigrant hysteria. We need immigrants for many different reasons, including as health-care workers. We can write all the government checks we want for health care, but it won't help us when we have a shortage of doctors and nurses, which is where we're heading—and anti-immigration policies are making that worse. We can see a warning of that in Britain, where a MAGA-style crackdown on immigration is endangering their national health care system. And contrary to claims made by Republicans, it is well documented that immigrants pay more into the American welfare system than they take out of it. Immigrants are helping pay for government benefits, and maybe we shouldn't be discouraging that.
**Up to 10 rural hospitals in Virginia have been listed as endangered. What would you propose to make sure they stay open?**
We need to restore the funding cut by HR1, but then also look at how we can adjust reimbursement rules to make sure rural hospitals remain viable.
**What are your views on immigration? Does the U.S. need more immigrants or fewer? What should be the criteria for entry and deportation? Under what circumstances should undocumented immigrants already here be given a pathway to citizenship?**
Donald Trump's anti-immigration policies are waking a lot of people up to the reality of immigration, because they show how his mass deportations are based on lies. He said he was going to target criminals and people who were violating the rules, but the majority of the people he has rounded up have no criminal records, and many were detained when they showed up for regular check-ins, precisely because they were trying to follow the rules. And many of them were loved and valued as members of their communities.

Trump's policies are shaped by hatred and xenophobia. They are not a reasonable response to legitimate concerns. There have been numerous studies showing that immigrants come here to work and contribute to our society, that they commit crimes at lower rates than the native born, and that they pay more into our welfare systems in taxes than they take out.

We've had previous anti-immigration hysterias in which demagogues vilified people with names like McGuire and names like Tracinski, and instead those people helped build this country and became as American as anybody else. We should clear the way for productive and law-abiding people to stay here, and immigration enforcement should go back to focusing on deporting dangerous criminals, not ordinary people who are just trying to make a better life for themselves and their families.

We should have more of an Ellis Island-style approach to immigration and oppose any policy that would have rejected our own grandparents or great-grandparents.
**Would you support an arms embargo on Israel? Why or why not? What else should we know about your views on Israel and Gaza?**
Decades ago, an Israeli friend warned me about Binyamin Netanyahu, pointing out that he presented two faces to the world. He came to America and in English said reasonable-sounding things about fighting terrorism—then he would go back to Israel and in Hebrew say things that supported the fanatical settler movement and its goal of ethnic cleansing against the Palestinians. That is exactly what has been playing out in his response to the October 7 terrorist attacks.
Israel has a right to exist, and I have no sympathy for terrorist organizations like Hamas and Hezbollah, which are highly repressive toward their own people and have their own murderous agenda. But that doesn't mean giving Netanyahu a blank check for a war that seems to have no strategy except as an excuse to kill Palestinians.
America has often been able to support Israel's legitimate claims while also using our support as leverage and not just a rubber stamp. We can do that again.
**What, if any, aid should the United States be supplying to Ukraine? Why or why not? What are the consequences if Russia succeeds in militarily claiming part of Ukraine?**
Full support for Ukraine—particularly air defense weapons and precision long-range artillery—is in American interests for three reasons.

First, Russian aggression against Ukraine threatens to return the world to the law of the jungle, a free-for-all in which the strong simply impose themselves on the weak. If Russia succeeds, we will face many more conflicts around the world than we do now. Every penny spent in Ukraine saves us dollars of future defense spending to deal with a more dangerous world.

Second, we owe Ukraine our support because they're fighting for democracy. Vladimir Putin developed the model of modern authoritarianism. He used politically connected "oligarchs" to control the media at home, while trying to intimidate Russia's neighbors and use its military power to carve off territory for his own aggrandizement. We can already see that when this model succeeds, it inspires imitators. We should support Ukraine to help ensure that the authoritarian model is revealed as a failure, in the same way the Cold War showed the failure of totalitarian communism and discredited the old Soviet model.
Third, we should support Ukraine because even without our full support, they're already winning, and in the process they are transforming modern warfare. Ukraine has become the world's drone superpower, mastering the new technology through innovation and constant trial-and-error on the battlefield.
We should be deeply concerned that the US military is falling behind--and the current administration is more concerned with getting corrupt defense contracts for Donald Trump, Jr., than with really modernizing our military.
Ukraine doesn't need an alliance with us as badly as we need an alliance with Ukraine, to help us modernize our military and learn the lessons of the new era of drone warfare.
**What, if anything, should the federal government do to either encourage or discourage development of artificial intelligence? Please address data centers as part of this.**
As a writer, I was once on the "emerging technology" beat and had to sift through a lot of Silicon Valley hype. The people who are saying AI is going to take over the world and take all our jobs predicted this was all going to happen by five years ago, so I think we should take both the promises and the fear with a giant grain of salt.

My greater worry is that circular financing in the AI industry is creating a multi-trillion-dollar bubble, and when it bursts, it will drag the real economy down with it.
I'm trying to help people find the best way to address real concerns about data centers without becoming Luddites. Most of the data centers in Virginia weren't built for AI. They were built so we can shop online and stream movies from Netflix. But if tech companies want to pour trillion into building new data centers, they should be required to pay their own way by building up the power and water infrastructure they need without pushing the costs onto consumers.
**President Trump has tried to block development of offshore wind energy. Dominion Energy is building an offshore wind facility off the coast of Virginia Beach and has long-range plans for more. What should the federal government's posture on offshore wind be? And energy development in general?**
We can always use an abundance of cheap and reliable power to drive down costs both for businesses and consumers.

It's reasonable to require power companies to mitigate negative effects like runoff and pollution, but not to discourage all development. We need what some people are calling "a liberalism that builds," because liberalism needs to show it can provide prosperity and not put unnecessary roadblocks in the way of progress.

Yet for all its rhetoric about being pro-energy, it is the Trump administration that is putting up the biggest barriers, fighting a war against solar and wind energy. Congress needs to fix a system that puts a thumb on the scale for fossil fuels—not coincidentally, Trump's donors—while actively blocking new sources of energy.

In the last decade, the price of solar energy and battery storage has been falling rapidly, making solar a cheaper, more practical, and reliable source—and one that could shield us from Trump's self-inflicted chaos in the Middle East.
**How would you assess the impact of the tariffs that President Trump has imposed?**
Tariffs always impose higher costs at home while starting trade wars that choke off markets for our own products.
A tariff on steel might be good for the relatively small number of workers at steel mills. But it raises costs for the far larger number of companies who use steel. This is why, for all of Trump's talk about reviving American industry, manufacturing jobs are down since he took office.
Meanwhile, farmers in Virginia are paying the price, too, because the trade war has cut off overseas markets for their crops.
The Constitution clearly gives Congress the power to set tariffs, yet Trump has declared that he can raise and lower them any time he likes. The courts have ruled these tariffs to be unconstitutional, but he keeps trying to find ways around the Constitution. This doesn't just damage our constitutional system. It also creates enormous economic uncertainty, so no one can plan ahead.
Congress needs to take back this power and stop the chaos.
**How would you assess the performance of President Trump? What actions would you take to support or oppose his agenda? For Democrats: Would you support impeachment? Why or why not?**
Trump has been a disaster. The economy isn't stronger, prices are higher, the American people are less safe from their own government, foreign dictators are emboldened, and Trump's war in the Middle East has left Iran in a stronger position than it was before.

Trump has only been effective at one thing: knocking down checks on his power, intimidating Republican in Congress into irrelevance, and centralizing all power in one person. But that is exactly the wrong thing.

Democrats in Congress should pass new laws to limit executive power and protect our constitutional rights—for example, stopping the FCC from threatening broadcast licenses. They should use Congress's control over spending as leverage to reassert its power.
Even if impeachment cannot remove Trump or his officials from office, the House should still attempt it just to bring his abuses of power to the attention of the American people and show that we do not accept the way he is changing our system of government.
**What changes, if any, to federal law would you like to see on abortion/contraception?**
We need a national law creating a reasonable minimum guarantee for reproductive rights.
The draconian abortion bans in Texas and elsewhere have demonstrated why overturning these protections was a mistake. Republican-controlled states have imposed laws that deny health care to pregnant women by making doctors, nurses, and hospitals afraid to deal with any serious complications. Women have suffered serious health problems, lost their fertility, and even died as a result.
Anyone who has had kids knows there are a lot of things that can go wrong in a pregnancy. Mothers, their spouses, and their doctors need to be able to make decisions based on the medical facts, not on the fear of being second-guessed by an overzealous prosecutor. Congress should pass a national protection for abortion rights that overrides these unnecessary and destructive state laws.
**What legislation, if any, would you support regarding firearms?**
I have made a promise to my friends and neighbors not to vote for any law that would make them or me a felon, which rules out the most radical gun-control proposals.

But also, the gun debate has evolved. At the height of the crime wave in the late 20th Century, the debate was about crime. Some thought we could stop violent crime by banning guns. Others argued that we needed the guns precisely to protect ourselves from crime.

Today, crime is back down to historically low levels, and many more of the deaths from firearms are a result of mental health struggles—suicides, especially among veterans, and school shootings. We should respond by focusing on more support for mental health while at the same time keeping guns out of the hands of unstable people.
**What else should voters know about you?**
I am not a traditional Democrat—15 to 20 years ago, I was active in the Tea Party movement in Charlottesville. I won't be down-the-line on every issue—which perhaps makes me a better fit for the Fifth District. Democrats here have a tendency to nominate candidates from the left-leaning Charlottesville area who have a hard time connecting with voters outside Albemarle County. I think I have an opportunity to change that, precisely because I'm not a traditional Democrat.

I signed up for the Democratic Party because of the "democracy" part, and I think that's something that can unify people across the district. I don't view this as a partisan campaign, but as a campaign for good old-fashioned Americanism and restoring the constitutional balance of powers.
I think I can even convince some conservatives--maybe a few of my old Tea Party friends--that they will really want more limitations on presidential power once they face the prospect of seeing someone they don't like in the White House.
Help me get this agenda out by[ donating with ActBlue](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rob-tracinski-1). Even $100 or $200 can make a difference, especially in these crucial final days of the primary.

First, Russian aggression against Ukraine threatens to return the world to the law of the jungle, a free-for-all in which the strong simply impose themselves on the weak. If Russia succeeds, we will face many more conflicts around the world than we do now. Every penny spent in Ukraine saves us dollars of future defense spending to deal with a more dangerous world. Second, we owe Ukraine our support because they're fighting for democracy. Vladimir Putin developed the model of modern authoritarianism. He used politically connected "oligarchs" to control the media at home, while trying to intimidate Russia's neighbors and use its military power to carve off territory for his own aggrandizement. We can already see that when this model succeeds, it inspires imitators. We should support Ukraine to help ensure that the authoritarian model is revealed as a failure, in the same way the Cold War showed the failure of totalitarian communism and discredited the old Soviet model. Third, we should support Ukraine because even without our full support, they're already winning, and in the process they are transforming modern warfare. Ukraine has become the world's drone superpower, mastering the new technology through innovation and constant trial-and-error on the battlefield. We should be deeply concerned that the US military is falling behind--and the current administration is more concerned with getting corrupt defense contracts for Donald Trump, Jr., than with really modernizing our military. Ukraine doesn't need an alliance with us as badly as we need an alliance with Ukraine, to help us modernize our military and learn the lessons of the new era of drone warfare. What, if anything, should the federal government do to either encourage or discourage development of artificial intelligence? Please address data centers as part of this. As a writer, I was once on the "emerging technology" beat and had to sift through a lot of Silicon Valley hype. The people who are saying AI is going to take over the world and take all our jobs predicted this was all going to happen by five years ago, so I think we should take both the promises and the fear with a giant grain of salt. My greater worry is that circular financing in the AI industry is creating a multi-trillion-dollar bubble, and when it bursts, it will drag the real economy down with it. I'm trying to help people find the best way to address real concerns about data centers without becoming Luddites. Most of the data centers in Virginia weren't built for AI. They were built so we can shop online and stream movies from Netflix. But if tech companies want to pour trillion into building new data centers, they should be required to pay their own way by building up the power and water infrastructure they need without pushing the costs onto consumers. President Trump has tried to block development of offshore wind energy. Dominion Energy is building an offshore wind facility off the coast of Virginia Beach and has long-range plans for more. What should the federal government's posture on offshore wind be? And energy development in general? We can always use an abundance of cheap and reliable power to drive down costs both for businesses and consumers. It's reasonable to require power companies to mitigate negative effects like runoff and pollution, but not to discourage all development. We need what some people are calling "a liberalism that builds," because liberalism needs to show it can provide prosperity and not put unnecessary roadblocks in the way of progress. Yet for all its rhetoric about being pro-energy, it is the Trump administration that is putting up the biggest barriers, fighting a war against solar and wind energy. Congress needs to fix a system that puts a thumb on the scale for fossil fuels—not coincidentally, Trump's donors—while actively blocking new sources of energy. In the last decade, the price of solar energy and battery storage has been falling rapidly, making solar a cheaper, more practical, and reliable source—and one that could shield us from Trump's self-inflicted chaos in the Middle East. How would you assess the impact of the tariffs that President Trump has imposed? Tariffs always impose higher costs at home while starting trade wars that choke off markets for our own products. A tariff on steel might be good for the relatively small number of workers at steel mills. But it raises costs for the far larger number of companies who use steel. This is why, for all of Trump's talk about reviving American industry, manufacturing jobs are down since he took office. Meanwhile, farmers in Virginia are paying the price, too, because the trade war has cut off overseas markets for their crops. The Constitution clearly gives Congress the power to set tariffs, yet Trump has declared that he can raise and lower them any time he likes. The courts have ruled these tariffs to be unconstitutional, but he keeps trying to find ways around the Constitution. This doesn't just damage our constitutional system. It also creates enormous economic uncertainty, so no one can plan ahead. Congress needs to take back this power and stop the chaos. How would you assess the performance of President Trump? What actions would you take to support or oppose his agenda? For Democrats: Would you support impeachment? Why or why not? Trump has been a disaster. The economy isn't stronger, prices are higher, the American people are less safe from their own government, foreign dictators are emboldened, and Trump's war in the Middle East has left Iran in a stronger position than it was before. Trump has only been effective at one thing: knocking down checks on his power, intimidating Republican in Congress into irrelevance, and centralizing all power in one person. But that is exactly the wrong thing. Democrats in Congress should pass new laws to limit executive power and protect our constitutional rights—for example, stopping the FCC from threatening broadcast licenses. They should use Congress's control over spending as leverage to reassert its power. Even if impeachment cannot remove Trump or his officials from office, the House should still attempt it just to bring his abuses of power to the attention of the American people and show that we do not accept the way he is changing our system of government. What changes, if any, to federal law would you like to see on abortion/contraception? We need a national law creating a reasonable minimum guarantee for reproductive rights. The draconian abortion bans in Texas and elsewhere have demonstrated why overturning these protections was a mistake. Republican-controlled states have imposed laws that deny health care to pregnant women by making doctors, nurses, and hospitals afraid to deal with any serious complications. Women have suffered serious health problems, lost their fertility, and even died as a result. Anyone who has had kids knows there are a lot of things that can go wrong in a pregnancy. Mothers, their spouses, and their doctors need to be able to make decisions based on the medical facts, not on the fear of being second-guessed by an overzealous prosecutor. Congress should pass a national protection for abortion rights that overrides these unnecessary and destructive state laws. What legislation, if any, would you support regarding firearms? I have made a promise to my friends and neighbors not to vote for any law that would make them or me a felon, which rules out the most radical gun-control proposals. But also, the gun debate has evolved. At the height of the crime wave in the late 20th Century, the debate was about crime. Some thought we could stop violent crime by banning guns. Others argued that we needed the guns precisely to protect ourselves from crime. Today, crime is back down to historically low levels, and many more of the deaths from firearms are a result of mental health struggles—suicides, especially among veterans, and school shootings. We should respond by focusing on more support for mental health while at the same time keeping guns out of the hands of unstable people. What else should voters know about you? I am not a traditional Democrat—15 to 20 years ago, I was active in the Tea Party movement in Charlottesville. I won't be down-the-line on every issue—which perhaps makes me a better fit for the Fifth District. Democrats here have a tendency to nominate candidates from the left-leaning Charlottesville area who have a hard time connecting with voters outside Albemarle County. I think I have an opportunity to change that, precisely because I'm not a traditional Democrat. I signed up for the Democratic Party because of the "democracy" part, and I think that's something that can unify people across the district. I don't view this as a partisan campaign, but as a campaign for good old-fashioned Americanism and restoring the constitutional balance of powers. I think I can even convince some conservatives--maybe a few of my old Tea Party friends--that they will really want more limitations on presidential power once they face the prospect of seeing someone they don't like in the White House. Help me get this agenda out by. Even $100 or $200 can make a difference, especially in these crucial final days of the primary. | | | | | Please commit your support for a Congress that will not just speak for the people of this district but protect all of our rights against an out-of-control federal government. [How Ownership Should Be Part of the American Dream](https://swo5c8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mgdIqSaoNrArYKLAB6S9ZfgJJpp-tTiAMGB3gVORuKizNnXytLz11YKiIEt4equy6MvpNfQKJW4PYRTigqUlQfYvDxntb3LLy6PSSu2md1udYhPGnLfq7IdQyHu4O1m1YuLAahdzh6E_Cz5hGTS3rSWSynGPBEF1i5CtOqIC3eJg48eIA5ZYSfayXTsuNShzhNfKMlCRuzt77QJfWPSqJRP-AGL7EmsqqYB1kTjk52Y=&c=hjzcxDYWb6D-hK9Oz8kuniMIk6BBb824VLd-uMpfp7hyuty84_xRNw==&ch=qOXD0z1f6cfppozAdqm13hcpseXwFepCsJ6E8U9EeAGHvWTDGpthNQ==)
---
When Barb and I got married in 1991, we had good government jobs. We had talked about homeownership as a near-term goal, and two years later, we made it happen. I was 32, and Barb was 29. Age-wise, we were spot on for the national average for new homebuyers at that time.
We bought a 3-bedroom, 1-bath, 1,100-square-foot house for $135,000. Adjusted for inflation, that house should cost a little over $310,000 today. Several websites estimate its current market value at over $450,000.
We have to accept the fact that over the last 40 years, the cost of home ownership has risen faster than inflation and far faster than income--placing home ownership out of reach for many Americans.
A lot of you will point out that the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act just passed. This bill will definitely help, but it could take as much as a decade for the ROAD to Housing Act to significantly improve the situation. We need to go farther...

📰 [Alabama environmental groups join lawsuit over pipeline permitting process](https://swo5c8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mgdIqSaoNrArYKLAB6S9ZfgJJpp-tTiAMGB3gVORuKizNnXytLz11YKiIEt4equyoBWDTbZC4L8K4BYGFhn79N158vV6fjz3TaMaR9vC-lKj__erUrVm2LAfjba9Tp4ZNoSDvV46YVN5Rg1G79xEBtezn6jPp0kDV4FDfU0C2yki0lqNIKPRLRBUDh7zyLN4nsQJ1U7mqE5oB87Zy4Jl7HuVVUrRb4bDBCTmfh7mEtvISZ4BoI5K_WtdlihFjGTVK0CaS_e9L7fP1p41reTF1g==&c=hjzcxDYWb6D-hK9Oz8kuniMIk6BBb824VLd-uMpfp7hyuty84_xRNw==&ch=qOXD0z1f6cfppozAdqm13hcpseXwFepCsJ6E8U9EeAGHvWTDGpthNQ==)
Environmental groups, including the Alabama Rivers Alliance and Black Warrior Riverkeeper, have sued the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, arguing that it is using a streamlined permitting process to approve large natural gas pipeline projects without thorough environmental review or meaningful public input. The lawsuit contends the proposed pipelines, which would cross 10 Alabama counties and thousands of waterways, could harm water quality, wildlife habitats, and endangered species, and should undergo project-specific environmental review before construction begins.
---
|
---
📰 [Many Alabama virtual school students lack basic math and reading skills, report cards show](https://swo5c8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mgdIqSaoNrArYKLAB6S9ZfgJJpp-tTiAMGB3gVORuKizNnXytLz11YKiIEt4equysCgl2NQKApWTqBzRVwz5bZxlze68KOO2b1aN9PuP4xYg8XijND6DTGEX7v70i2zTKQ3Y1cydq9x80agmGxltetXKXrZwmmw53T1uFilbt32gg-pdPbE-_Xro98Hv1XdUy0aidO26siv_FQ0xEOih9T0KiDBHhtpcFCZXEZ0YoZcHwgX-_MjJyZUgkhO-76YdLh0ekgeSefWOuGSCPktUzJEiGpQzZVibK9dQaMrXhFU=&c=hjzcxDYWb6D-hK9Oz8kuniMIk6BBb824VLd-uMpfp7hyuty84_xRNw==&ch=qOXD0z1f6cfppozAdqm13hcpseXwFepCsJ6E8U9EeAGHvWTDGpthNQ==)
An analysis of Alabama's 2024-25 school report cards found that many virtual schools have low reading and math proficiency rates, with some of the state's largest online schools reporting fewer than 10% of students proficient in math. State education leaders are calling for a review of virtual school enrollment, funding, and academic performance, while school officials say they are expanding tutoring, live instruction, and targeted interventions to improve student outcomes.
---
|
---
📰 [Data centers emerge as top Alabama election issue as community concerns grow](https://swo5c8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mgdIqSaoNrArYKLAB6S9ZfgJJpp-tTiAMGB3gVORuKizNnXytLz11YKiIEt4equymCl7FFspOpQ14qRnS2pSmUNKVe0-BLWaR8fMIMNnNOg21DwwnmgclUusd38Kx4-aV32hnw7xvxgRrVJeHjXs3d9ujac83oHIOLGkMXPbZcv_nZgz2Tatqv0orSxHvgRree5IAjb2ttnSwLsGgiBiRcbL4FcW4aYXAqtNAC3ZvntRh5wyU81RXgDHynt14Pc_-2AXGTSzSxnCK93VNWHTnffPVs2VobWU&c=hjzcxDYWb6D-hK9Oz8kuniMIk6BBb824VLd-uMpfp7hyuty84_xRNw==&ch=qOXD0z1f6cfppozAdqm13hcpseXwFepCsJ6E8U9EeAGHvWTDGpthNQ==)
Data centers have become a major issue in Alabama's elections as communities raise concerns about transparency, environmental impacts, water and power usage, and quality of life. While some candidates support expanding data centers for economic growth and national security, others are calling for a temporary moratorium and stronger public oversight, arguing that current state law limits Alabama's ability to regulate the facilities or address residents' concerns.

---
First, we need you to get the word out. This is a grassroots campaign which means we're going to rely heavily on you. Second, we need to meet your friends. One asset we have in this campaign is a candidate who will meet with people and have a conversation. Sometimes those conversations can be tough, but they're always productive. Set up a group meeting either in person (which is great) or virtually (which is also great). Email [joinus@leemcinnis4alabama.com](mailto:joinus@leemcinnis4alabama.com) to let us know where you are, and we'll work out the details with you.

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
As we look ahead, one thing is clear: real change begins in our neighborhoods, our communities, and with people who decide to make it happen.

Every conversation with a neighbor, every town hall or democratic party meeting attended, every yard sign placed, every question asked, and every volunteer who steps up to help builds a movement. Your voice matters. When you speak up, stay informed, and participate, you are shaping the future for countless families and the next generation.

Whether you've attended an event, shared our message with a friend, or are thinking about getting involved for the first time, thank you for being part of this effort. This campaign is powered by people who believe their community deserves to be heard.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

clean_body: You Don't Want to Miss This | | | | | == | | | CAMPAIGN UPDATE | | | | | | == | MAKING HISTORY | | THE WEEK AHEAD | | Food Trucks in LaFayette 🗓️ August 5 🕓 5 - 9:00 P.M. 📍LaFayette | | Prayer on the Square at the LaFayette Court House 🗓️ August 7 🕓 6:00 P.M. 📍LaFayette Court House | | | Tallapoosa County Town Hall 🗓️ August 8 🕓 2- 4 P.M. 📍 Sportsplex Cabin 1685 Arena Rd Alexander City | | | | | THE WEEK BEHIND | | | | | | | | | On Tuesday night, we held our first Veterans Beer Call in Opelika. It was a chance to bring veterans together, share a few stories, and discuss the issues that concerned them. We'd like to have more all over the district but we'll need your help getting the locations. Let us know if you're willing to help. | | | | | | | On Thursday, the Tallapoosa County Democratic Party held a meeting in Wall Street. If you don't know, Wall Street is just outside of Tallassee. We had a good group, and I saw the same thing I've seen so many times. People frustrated with the direction the country is moving in and who can't even get their elected representatives on the phone to tell them how they feel. | | | | | | | When I was meeting with the great people of Wall Street, Barb was meeting Alabama's next First Lady and spent the evening with the democratic women of Lee County. | | | | | | | Leaving Wall Street, my voice was a little rough. When I woke up on Friday, it was gone. I could barely speak. But we had promised good people at the Fresh Oil Full Gospel Church that we would show up for their Big Wheels and Big Faith Community Adventure Trails celebration. Barb jumped in, and for the next two days, I got nothing but great feedback on how happy people were to have her. | | | | | | | The AFL-CIO met to determine which candidates they would endorse for this year's election. So in addition to talking to a lot of great union members, it was a chance to hang out with just about every other candidate in the state. | | | In Case You Missed It | | BLOG POSTS | == When Barb and I got married in 1991, we had good government jobs. We had talked about homeownership as a near-term goal, and two years later, we made it happen. I was 32, and Barb was 29. Age-wise, we were spot on for the national average for new homebuyers at that time. We bought a 3-bedroom, 1-bath, 1,100-square-foot house for $135,000. Adjusted for inflation, that house should cost a little over $310,000 today. Several websites estimate its current market value at over $450,000. We have to accept the fact that over the last 40 years, the cost of home ownership has risen faster than inflation and far faster than income--placing home ownership out of reach for many Americans. A lot of you will point out that the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act just passed. This bill will definitely help, but it could take as much as a decade for the ROAD to Housing Act to significantly improve the situation. We need to go farther... | == | A Few Things to Think About | | | ALABAMA IN THE NEWS | 📰 == Environmental groups, including the Alabama Rivers Alliance and Black Warrior Riverkeeper, have sued the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, arguing that it is using a streamlined permitting process to approve large natural gas pipeline projects without thorough environmental review or meaningful public input. The lawsuit contends the proposed pipelines, which would cross 10 Alabama counties and thousands of waterways, could harm water quality, wildlife habitats, and endangered species, and should undergo project-specific environmental review before construction begins. | 📰 == An analysis of Alabama's 2024-25 school report cards found that many virtual schools have low reading and math proficiency rates, with some of the state's largest online schools reporting fewer than 10% of students proficient in math. State education leaders are calling for a review of virtual school enrollment, funding, and academic performance, while school officials say they are expanding tutoring, live instruction, and targeted interventions to improve student outcomes. | 📰 == Data centers have become a major issue in Alabama's elections as communities raise concerns about transparency, environmental impacts, water and power usage, and quality of life. While some candidates support expanding data centers for economic growth and national security, others are calling for a temporary moratorium and stronger public oversight, arguing that current state law limits Alabama's ability to regulate the facilities or address residents' concerns. | A CALL TO ACTION | As we come down to the last three months, we need you to do four things: First, we need you to get the word out. This is a grassroots campaign which means we're going to rely heavily on you. Share our posts, talk to your friends, and show off those yard signs and bumper stickers. If you don't have a yard sign, email mailto:joinus@leemcinnis4alabama.comto let us know what county you're in, and we'll hook you up with the person in your county who has some. == == == | Second, we need to meet your friends. One asset we have in this campaign is a candidate who will meet with people and have a conversation. Sometimes those conversations can be tough, but they're always productive. Set up a group meeting either in person (which is great) or virtually (which is also great). Email mailto:joinus@leemcinnis4alabama.com to let us know where you are, and we'll work out the details with you. | | | Third, make a plan to vote. We don't know what is going to happen between now and November 3, but the best way to ensure a free and fair election is to show up in huge numbers. Once you have your plan, help your friends and neighbors plan to vote. | | | Fourth, donate to the campaign. You have all been incredibly generous financially, but we are entering the expense phase of this race. Barb and I haven't charged the campaign for gas, meals, or hotel rooms so that we could save money for these last 90 days. Without corporate or foreign-interest PAC money, we knew we would have to run a slim campaign, but now we have to start getting our name in front of a wider audience, and that will require capital. | | == | | One Last Thought Until Next Week | | | As we look ahead, one thing is clear: real change begins in our neighborhoods, our communities, and with people who decide to make it happen. Every conversation with a neighbor, every town hall or democratic party meeting attended, every yard sign placed, every question asked, and every volunteer who steps up to help builds a movement. Your voice matters. When you speak up, stay informed, and participate, you are shaping the future for countless families and the next generation. Whether you've attended an event, shared our message with a friend, or are thinking about getting involved for the first time, thank you for being part of this effort. This campaign is powered by people who believe their community deserves to be heard. Coming soon: Calhoun County Town Hall Train Depot in Jacksonville August 11, 6-8:00PM Lee County Town Hall Opelika Public Library August 20, 6-8:00PM Next week, we will be under 90 days away from the election. We're going to have to start asking for help in some key areas. It's about to get busy. We are 91 days away from the general election. It's officially Primary Election Day, and there's only one thing left to do: vote, vote, vote.

Today, voters have a clear choice.

Wesley has spent his career standing up for the people of St. Louis — not the powerful, not the well-connected, but the families who deserve someone who will fight for them every single day.

**[If you haven't voted yet, make your plan now and cast your ballot for Congressman Wesley Bell. You can find your polling place here>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136569427/637911708/1036245226?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzVhZTBkYTQtZjM4Zi1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CDw6iVPg-Js0dsVLpribAZ8pjjYKR-6GMzecNOsDqSY=&emci=835b34ad-e48c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=35ae0da4-f38f-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1020964)**

**That's the kind of leadership we need now, more than ever.** Wesley has proven that he'll do the work, listen to the people he serves, and put our community first. Gov. His letter to the Public Utility Commission of Texas and ERCOT requires developers to [disclose tax breaks](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdEa28R1c4SIN3aVNidbsAlYMRvbmOP4-Ir-QZqqnmdH7eg5PCDFs8yes5Pg9pWGjo0Ripjx8wzln2GbKGKiUcUkpliXt-2CUuUvVSWUHhBDPwVbovMKHrsjptrt1VjdtUy0OpxFGbb1v2pv2oBAfWiOg7TwZO6kquKtMdcpqrcxN18b6VisC8kajgUZYRRg45ZoXYnpDmeKZXpTrMa1VdAvzXkTzIUwvTH8cRz2FXBgiZW4vRpj-mhCmV90VjTA9eJ-YZcpIuUhaKc-0jaeEHwxcJMQod9owbLNEYJAjbXyRhYHpCEjC9FV2uB8hxlDurbBqXiHEv1P8P5UvZ34DAAD__yOGiiQ), power and water use, cooling technology, ownership, and noise and light controls. Peter – we'll get right to the point.
**Experts say that Democrats have no shot at flipping the U.S. Senate without winning in North Carolina.** This is one of the most important Senate races in the country, and like all elections in this critical swing state, it’s going to be decided by a razor-thin margin.

body:
His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible.

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c9q3DAQBvCnkW82Y0m2lYMPCc5CIWnpH8hRKKOxPSBLxpI35O3Lli303OvMMD_4vrdX--o4cFy-uo1Gztn65K3njOlKR1npndxZPl305TjLaiXIvgZTg7YOC1_Jalf5sZOtmU1FYzuYzugOhqFaR4WzHGTfd8rgAEZ3Es0Dtb2WaHro3iseb__AgG4laNU1mjS8O4ly8Aq8moWGc_euUMMxs6eMKe17ClwYc5OOpQrjWsqehXoU8iLkheOcmpVDyN4FasifQl7mg6jGXAf64FzjenAu7CKXz9pfvVCXjEJNAFKqRwBoX9qH6ds0Pf8Usj_LZnM6DyShpv1IeScsHJf7aiPP5ybURJvjcB-i23bHSxRqwmz_qPZf1d7U-2mKhWIRanr68vTybL8P9duvH_XfXKpj9PsHh8C5H4SG5aY0mLaq_G9b11H-DgAA__9at6ZP)

Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c9q3DAQBvCnkW82Y0m2lYMPCc5CIWnpH8hRKKOxPSBLxpI35O3Lli303OvMMD_4vrdX--o4cFy-uo1Gztn65K3njOlKR1npndxZPl305TjLaiXIvgZTg7YOC1_Jalf5sZOtmU1FYzuYzugOhqFaR4WzHGTfd8rgAEZ3Es0Dtb2WaHro3iseb__AgG4laNU1mjS8O4ly8Aq8moWGc_euUMMxs6eMKe17ClwYc5OOpQrjWsqehXoU8iLkheOcmpVDyN4FasifQl7mg6jGXAf64FzjenAu7CKXz9pfvVCXjEJNAFKqRwBoX9qH6ds0Pf8Usj_LZnM6DyShpv1IeScsHJf7aiPP5ybURJvjcB-i23bHSxRqwmz_qPZf1d7U-2mKhWIRanr68vTybL8P9duvH_XfXKpj9PsHh8C5H4SG5aY0mLaq_G9b11H-DgAA__9at6ZP)

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. Lewis and Michael Ward with this beautiful free DVD set.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c9q3DAQBvCnkW82Y0m2lYMPCc5CIWnpH8hRKKOxPSBLxpI35O3Lli303OvMMD_4vrdX--o4cFy-uo1Gztn65K3njOlKR1npndxZPl305TjLaiXIvgZTg7YOC1_Jalf5sZOtmU1FYzuYzugOhqFaR4WzHGTfd8rgAEZ3Es0Dtb2WaHro3iseb__AgG4laNU1mjS8O4ly8Aq8moWGc_euUMMxs6eMKe17ClwYc5OOpQrjWsqehXoU8iLkheOcmpVDyN4FasifQl7mg6jGXAf64FzjenAu7CKXz9pfvVCXjEJNAFKqRwBoX9qH6ds0Pf8Usj_LZnM6DyShpv1IeScsHJf7aiPP5ybURJvjcB-i23bHSxRqwmz_qPZf1d7U-2mKhWIRanr68vTybL8P9duvH_XfXKpj9PsHh8C5H4SG5aY0mLaq_G9b11H-DgAA__9at6ZP)

Warm regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

**P.S.** You probably know that C.S. Lewis also wrote the children's series, _The Chronicles of Narnia_. My wife and I read those books to our children so many times! I can't tell you how many dog-eared copies we have of these.

One of the best parts of this course is learning how the Christian faith is woven into these captivating stories. **I hope you 'll take advantage of this great FREE DVD offer today:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c9q3DAQBvCnkW82Y0m2lYMPCc5CIWnpH8hRKKOxPSBLxpI35O3Lli303OvMMD_4vrdX--o4cFy-uo1Gztn65K3njOlKR1npndxZPl305TjLaiXIvgZTg7YOC1_Jalf5sZOtmU1FYzuYzugOhqFaR4WzHGTfd8rgAEZ3Es0Dtb2WaHro3iseb__AgG4laNU1mjS8O4ly8Aq8moWGc_euUMMxs6eMKe17ClwYc5OOpQrjWsqehXoU8iLkheOcmpVDyN4FasifQl7mg6jGXAf64FzjenAu7CKXz9pfvVCXjEJNAFKqRwBoX9qH6ds0Pf8Usj_LZnM6DyShpv1IeScsHJf7aiPP5ybURJvjcB-i23bHSxRqwmz_qPZf1d7U-2mKhWIRanr68vTybL8P9duvH_XfXKpj9PsHh8C5H4SG5aY0mLaq_G9b11H-DgAA__9at6ZP)

name: Chris Deluzio
subject: I was born there
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Deluzio for Congress
body:
Solidarity.
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=45%2E42639%2ElRIKwV)
Let me start by saying something many of you probably already know. And that is, today in this country, the game is rigged against workers trying to form a union and bargain for a fair contract.
This is true in almost all sectors, including those where working conditions can impact the health and welfare of all of us.
Take the UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital.
If you are from the area, you are familiar. I was born at that hospital. Almost half of the births in Allegheny County happen there. They care for more than 1,500 severely or critically ill babies a year.
Right now, a group of about 900 nurses and advanced practitioners at the hospital are fighting for a fair contract, but have been met with 8 months of stalling, delays, and bad faith bargaining.
And what are some of the radical things those nurses and others in the unit are asking for?
Fair wages and more staff. They want–at UPMC's most profitable hospital–an appropriate number of staff to deal with the families they care for on a daily basis.
I met with a number of the hospital workers last week, and I wanted to share a little bit more information about their struggle with you.
**[Watch it here:](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/367?t=2&akid=45%2E42639%2ElRIKwV)**
[](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/367?t=3&akid=45%2E42639%2ElRIKwV)
I know... this isn't your usual political email. Very true. But support from the community and allies everywhere is a powerful tool in these fights where workers have the deck stacked against them.
So I hope you'll watch the video above. Drive up its view count. Maybe send a message of support online about the struggle.
Thanks for reading.
In solidarity,
Chris Deluzio

* * *

☀️ Wait ... Before you click away! 🇺🇸

Unfortunately, not everyone gives—so he's counting on people like you who know the stakes in this election to chip-in what they can.

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SEAN MCCANN FOR CONGRESS
body:
I’m headed out the door to cast my ballot before a busy day of talking to voters, but first I wanted to personally reach out.

Hi folks, It’s Sean. I’m headed out the door to cast my ballot before a busy day of talking to voters, but first I wanted to personally reach out about my race. Recent data is reaffirming what we’ve known all along: this race is winnable. The latest polling shows us leading Bill Huizenga by 3 points. Election forecasters have upgraded our chances of flipping this seat and found this race is a true toss-up, on track to be decided by less than a 1% margin. That’s not by chance. That’s because of the hard work, determination, and grit this team has shown for the past year. Whether you’ve donated, volunteered, or simply kept up with emails like this one: **thank you! ** **Because of you, we’re building a campaign that has what it’ll take to win in November. ** But we can’t get complacent. name: Alex Vindman
subject: The choices I’ve made
body:
When I decided to run for this Senate seat, I had no idea what to expect.
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1317?t=1&akid=986%2E3892029%2E_fxB3E)

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em260804-1&refcode2=986_3892029__fxB3E&akid=986%2E3892029%2E_fxB3E)
---
Our campaign has sent a lot of emails, and this one explains my decision to run for Senate and why your support is so important to our success.
The truth is, when I decided to run for this Senate seat, I had no idea what to expect. Some friends and family were encouraging me to run and my brother had just won his House race in Virginia, but I had no idea what the reception would be if I jumped in to run in Florida... a place that has been tough for Democrats lately.
But I thought about this decision like I did when I blew the whistle on Donald Trump's not-so-perfect phone call with Ukraine. The one that led to his first impeachment.
I risked everything by reporting that phone call. I didn't do it for political gain. I did it to protect our democracy. I know I served my nation by helping expose corruption by the President.
It is in that spirit I decided to run for Senate.
And if we can win this seat, we'll ensure Democrats can take a (slight!) majority and pass legislation that protects our democracy from any current and future wannabe tyrant.
To be direct: Getting within the margin of error in Florida has taken a lot of resources. And I've done it without raising a single dollar from corporate PACs. But with the elections coming up fast, I need you more than ever.

I grew up in a working-class family in Allagash.
We didn’t always have heat or running water. Sometimes, we relied on food assistance to make ends meet.
My dad was a logger out in the woods, and one day he and his fellow loggers had to stand up to a wealthy landowner who was threatening their wages. They weren’t even asking for more money, they just wanted to be paid fairly.
“Take the pay cut or go home,” they were told.
I’ll never forget that day. I was only 11 years old, and watched my dad fight for something bigger than all of us — a basic fairness every worker should be entitled to, the ability to make ends meet, the ability to put food on the table for their family.
I know what it’s like to worry about paying the bills on time. I know what it’s like to fight, not just for your own future, but for the future of everyone around you, too.
And it’s that fight I’ll bring to the United States Senate. For too long, our voices have been ignored and crushed by powerful corporations and special interests who make backroom deals with greedy politicians.
Now’s our chance to change that. NAME, we have less than 100 days to build a campaign big enough to defeat Susan Collins. But with your help today, I know we can do it. I promise you I’ll spend every day in the Senate fighting for you and your families.

name: The Democrats
subject: You are not a credit card
body:
---
Derek, we’re sure you receive emails from other organizations and campaigns. If you do, you’ve probably gotten _plenty_ of emails that sound like they’re trying to rush you into giving a donation. You’ve probably received even more than usual in the past few days. **So we wanted to reach out today and remind you what the DNC stands for:**
* **You are _not_ just a credit card, a wallet, or an ATM we run to when we need money.** Every grassroots supporter who receives our emails is a valued member of our team — whether you’re a donor, a volunteer, or just keeping up with our work to elect Democrats.
* The point of our emails is _never_ to make you feel scared or rushed into giving. We want you to be fully informed of all of the different ways we’re working to elect Democrats so you can contribute when the time feels right for you.
* Our goal is to always make sure you know exactly where your money goes — we want to provide you with accurate, up-to-date information about our organizing programs, our legal work, our voter protection initiatives and more.

**In short: When we reach out to our supporters, we’re reaching out because we genuinely value your contribution to this team — in whatever form it may come.** The DNC is fueled by grassroots supporters, not the ultra-wealthy, and every contribution we receive represents another Democrat who is ready to stand up and fight back. [**So Derek, when you get an email from us asking for your support, this is exactly the kind of intention and thoughtful consideration that goes into each message. We appreciate all the support you’ve given Democrats so far this year, and hope you’ll consider chipping in $7 today. It's time to vote!
| | | | Hi Friend,
**Today is primary election day!******Polls are open now to 7pm, and _I'd be honored to have your vote._
This campaign has been about one thing from day one: restoring faith in the American Dream for every family in VA-10. Today, you get to help make that real.
We have a lot at stake this election season, like the DSA agenda creeping into our own backyard, prevalent fraud draining our entitlement programs, and election integrity concerns putting trust in our system at risk.

VA-10 needs a congressman who's ready to fight against the fraudsters, who will consistently vote against wasteful spending, and who will unequivocally defend our Constitution. **After 30 years serving and fighting for this country, I'm ready to step up and be that congressman.**
I've spent my life in service to this country and this community. Now I'm asking for your vote so I can bring that same service to Congress and fight for VA-10's American Dream.

I can't thank you enough for standing with me throughout this campaign. Your vote today gets us one step closer to taking this fight to Suhas in the fall, Friend.
Find your polling place here: [www.elections.virginia.gov/casting-a-ballot/polling-place-lookup/](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

subject: 🤔 Mansharamani Musings for July: Review of Vikram's latest thoughts 💭
body:
A review of Vikram's July posts...

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mansharamani/vikram-update-july-17451133?e=93b2c2b824)
---
[|
---](http://www.mansharamani.com)
| | | | | |
# Mansharamani Musings
---
| | [](http://mansharamani.substack.com)During July, I spoke with leaders from various industries and across many geographies. The five biggest topics of interest I encountered in July were (1) geopolitics and the Iran War...but with increasing curiosity about the future of Cuba, (2) how the new round of tariffs and energy price volatility will impact the outlook for inflation and the Fed’s response, (3) whether artificial intelligence infrastructure was a bubble about to burst, (4) Chinese economic weakness and whether it was driven by lower energy usage during the second quarter, and (5) how the increasing commercialization of space will impact sectors on earth. Best wishes for a thought-filled August!_**
- Vikram**_

---
[|
---](https://mansharamani.substack.com/p/america-at-250-still-shining)
| | **JULY 4, 2026**

Inspired by my attendance at a naturalization ceremony in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, two years ago, I have been writing about America each year around Independence Day. Spending the day of America’s birth with her newest citizens, it was impossible for me not to think about my own family’s immigrant journey, and each year I pause and reflect with gratitude about our great nation.

Last year, in “[Still a Shining City on a Hill](https://mansharamani.substack.com/p/still-a-shining-city-on-a-hill),” I wrote about my family’s journey, in particular that of my father, who traveled from India to Africa to a little apartment in Queens to the life he built in New Jersey. This year, as America turns 250, I suspect it will not surprise readers to learn that I am as convinced as ever that the United States is still the greatest nation on Earth. Despite political headlines and polarized dogma, America is still shining. More so than ever, actually...

---
| [CLICK HERE TO CONTINUE READING](https://mansharamani.substack.com/p/america-at-250-still-shining)
---
|
---
[|
---](https://mansharamani.substack.com/p/tick-tick-tick)
| | **July 12, 2026**

I have spent a career arguing that the most important signals rarely announce themselves. The skyscraper that tops out at the market peak. The pizza order that spikes in the Pentagon parking lot the night before a military operation. The private-label, single-serve trade-down in the frozen aisle that telegraphs a stressed consumer months before the macro data confirm it. Connecting seemingly irrelevant dots is not a parlor trick. It is, I’d argue, the only reliable way to see around corners and navigate uncertainty.
And the latest dot that has caught my eye is the size of a poppy seed that no one on Wall Street is watching: **a tick that is quietly building a short position in animal protein.** At the root of the development is a disease the tick spreads. It’s a condition called [alpha-gal syndrome](https://www.cdc.gov/alpha-gal-syndrome/about/index.html), or AGS, for short. It is an allergy (often severe, sometimes fatal) — to a sugar present in almost every non-primate mammal. AGS essentially makes you allergic to meat...
---
| [CLICK HERE TO CONTINUE READING](https://mansharamani.substack.com/p/tick-tick-tick)
---
|
---
[|
---](https://mansharamani.substack.com/p/lessons-from-the-pitch)
| | **July 19, 2026**

The World Cup final is later today (Argentina and the legendary Messi versus Spain and Lamine Yamal) at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey—and I’ll be watching. My son is an avid soccer fan and watching the games together has been one of those family moments you don’t plan but never forget. Sitting on the couch, cheering for the home team (or the favorite...or the underdog...), groaning at bad calls, high-fiving after goals, with the most important people in my world. And of course, how could we not fall in love with the Norwegian viking row...

As I watched the games this year, I was reminded of Franklin Foer’s book [_How Soccer Explains the World_](https://www.amazon.com/How-Soccer-Explains-World-Globalization/dp/0063486768/ref=sr_1_1?dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.P156pCs7rGFFbkWwOwNuBYR-oNQUSDseQ-DIMbiBMR84zHyhifd4o-RR2z9zxEkXlw9sA4QIO_h3RWBDlfUpZYW3FyL_8qIVMofdq7HJ2MMCaq0ZazRCxB3ZFHL1C2JzgoU7In8DyhYHdmDHyvJCZTYcrnjGDC3JdGsBuO34kSqKh04GiJmIY8xOPY367C5Eb0Nike9RdjdEniiIN83vFkHiXAHsoCUEmTzdXeSFd8g.jnJroTrra-mIkRdhWKnN_WKPM--slc9eQzzG_9NvN6k&dib_tag=se&hvadid=792761845106&hvdev=c&hvexpln=67&hvlocphy=1021943&hvnetw=g&hvocijid=14807233911863312062--&hvqmt=e&hvrand=14807233911863312062&hvtargid=kwd-364855210037&hydadcr=4578_13551753&keywords=how+soccer+explains+the+world&mcid=8092c25bf9c0357782bdba4a09804243&qid=1784319886&sr=8-1) , which came out in 2004 and used soccer as a lens to explain tribalism, nationalism, corruption, and the enduring power of identity. It was a contrarian book during an era when Thomas Friedman’s [_The World Is Flat_](https://www.amazon.com/World-Flat-History-Twenty-first-Century/dp/0374292884/ref=sr_1_2?crid=Z0TPRSESWJTB&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.H4jHDdjYcmhDTX-W9vTOsdZZx5_L0dCmMEpXo416y_qCAybGemGZjsdHYsqEfC38Ckqlc-dm0NUGYujLdBVAxyAvF81C_s1di9Ol9MjbIh1p6nS7b1hLqYMMPxZj5OB5ZTAdClNh2yS1Xs4QUEkPrfaKva9gPUT5JfVdvkiQUuk7VK0dHxuXbmjJVHolfxGRQ0TzerwyC757AexfxQyt4XaIAKKimntiJdzZvIix71Y.mh9UrRjz3AESAzZ6ivXZ2Go3KAsToG0va03hUE9X5-E&dib_tag=se&keywords=the+world+is+flat&qid=1784319940&sprefix=the+world+is+fla%2Caps%2C217&sr=8-2) (2005) was on everyone’s mind, when globalization was supposed to sand down every rough edge and turn the world into one big market. Who could forget his famous thesis that no two countries that had a McDonald’s had ever gone to war with each other?
Foer pushed back. His argument was that the Beautiful Game revealed something uglier underneath. Foer suggested that tribalism doesn’t dissolve with free trade but rather deepens. Familiarity breeds contempt, as the old saying goes...
---
| [CLICK HERE TO CONTINUE READING](https://mansharamani.substack.com/p/lessons-from-the-pitch)
---
|
---
[|
---](https://mansharamani.substack.com/p/pork-politics-and-pepperoni-pizza)
| | **JULY 26, 2026**

As many of you are aware, I run a frozen pizza factory. Pepperoni pizza is one of our best sellers, so it should not be surprising that I spend a lot of time thinking about pork prices. And while the price of your pizza is obviously impacted by the price of pepperoni on top of it, you may find it interesting that the price is increasingly being set in Beijing, not in Iowa or North Carolina.
How’s that? Well, it turns out that the Middle Kingdom is the world’s largest consumer of pork. China consumes [57 million metric tons of pork per year](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2025/03/18/us-china-pork-trade-war/)—roughly **half of all the pork eaten on Earth**. And pork in China isn’t like chicken in America. The Chinese character for “home” (家) is literally a pig under a roof and pork is deeply intertwined with Chinese culture. So when anything disrupts China’s pork supply (such as a disease, tariff, or trade war), shockwaves flow through global markets. Including, eventually, to the pepperoni we put on pizzas in America....
---

As I have in the past, I’m addressing a wide range of topics, ranging from geopolitics and economics to social trends to technology. Self-taught to think around corners and connect original dots, he spends his time speaking with global leaders in business, government, academia, and journalism. **He’s currently the Chairman and CEO of Goodwell Foods, a manufacturer of private label frozen pizza**. _LinkedIn_ has twice listed him as its #1 Top Voice in Money & Finance, and _Worth_ profiled him as one of the 100 Most Powerful People in Global Finance. Vikram earned a PhD From MIT, has taught at Yale and Harvard, and is the author of three books, [ _**The Making of a Generalist: An Independent Thinker Finds Unconventional Success in an Uncertain World**_](https://amzn.to/3DCd7E0) , [ _**Think for Yourself: Restoring Common Sense in an Age of Experts and Artificial Intelligence**_](https://amzn.to/3NSX6Mc) and [ _**Boombustology: Spotting Financial Bubbles Before They Burst**_](https://amzn.to/3NUuGBs). Who could forget his famous thesis that no two countries that had a McDonald’s had ever gone to war with each other? Foer pushed back. His argument was that the Beautiful Game revealed something uglier underneath. Foer suggested that tribalism doesn’t dissolve with free trade but rather deepens. Familiarity breeds contempt, as the old saying goes... | | | | JULY 26, 2026 As many of you are aware, I run a frozen pizza factory. Pepperoni pizza is one of our best sellers, so it should not be surprising that I spend a lot of time thinking about pork prices. And while the price of your pizza is obviously impacted by the price of pepperoni on top of it, you may find it interesting that the price is increasingly being set in Beijing, not in Iowa or North Carolina. How’s that? Well, it turns out that the Middle Kingdom is the world’s largest consumer of pork. China consumes —roughly half of all the pork eaten on Earth. And pork in China isn’t like chicken in America. The Chinese character for “home” (家) is literally a pig under a roof and pork is deeply intertwined with Chinese culture. So when anything disrupts China’s pork supply (such as a disease, tariff, or trade war), shockwaves flow through global markets. subject: Good morning and happy primary election day, Peter

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=2830%2E251025%2ER5skpy ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=2830%2E251025%2ER5skpy ]Abdul for US Senate

Good morning,
Peter.

It's Election Day in Michigan. I've been up since 5 AM — first espresso
already gone — and I wanted to write to you before the day gets away from
me.

A year ago, this campaign was a handful of us in a room, a website, and a
theory: that Michigan could send someone to the Senate who's never taken a
dollar from a corporate PAC, who wrote the book on Medicare for All, who
actually believes government should work for people instead of donors.

That theory only survives if people show up for it. You did.

We’ve brought this movement to every corner of Michigan, meeting with
folks who are sick and tired of the status quo and are ready for change.

We’ve made so many friends along the way — United Auto Workers, National
Nurses United, countless senators and representatives, local leaders, and
hundreds of thousands of
everyday folks,
including you,
Peter.

And now, we’re in a strong position to win the Democratic nomination,
because people like you decided that a campaign that answers to voters
instead of corporate PACs is worth fighting for.

I’m feeling so hopeful and grateful for what we’ve built together. Thank
you for being a part of this.

But we’ve still got work to do. If you can pitch in today, it goes
straight to reaching last-minute voters, who could be the deciding factor
in who moves on to the general election.

Abdul

subject: 2018, 2020, 2021... and 2026
disclaimer_text: Paid for by State Democrats Committee (StateDemocrats
body:
In 2018, Democrats worked to keep building on their lead – and together, they took their lead from 4% in May to 8% in July. In 2026, it’s been the reverse...
#
Hey Peter,
In the 2018 elections, Democrats took control of the House. In 2020, Democrats took back the White House. And just a few months later in 2021, the Georgia runoff gave Democrats the Senate.
That wave of victory has a real impact on the lives of millions of Americans. But in 2024, the Trump GOP fought back – and they peeled much of that progress away.
Now in 2026, after Democrats have already overworked in elections across the country, it’d be easy to think things are already heading in the right direction. But if the last ten years should have taught us anything, it’s that **we CANNOT afford to take anything for granted.**
**[That’s why today, we’re asking you to chip in toward efforts to support Democrats across the country. A dip in support means we’ll have fewer resources to send this fall toward key races that will decide control of the House and Senate. name: Adam Schiff
subject: 10 ways Trump has failed us.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Blue Amp Action
body:
| Every American deserves to know this
---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2756%2E259176%2EjEUbGv) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2756%2E259176%2EjEUbGv)_

Peter, this is Adam Schiff. Blue Amp Action said I could reach out. I’m not going to sugarcoat it: We’re up against a movement that’s determined to tear down our democracy and a man in the White House who’ll do anything to expand his power. [**We’ve got to keep calling out the danger — that’s why I’m reaching out today to ask you to chip in to my campaign and Blue Amp Action to help me keep fighting back against Trump’s attacks on the rule of law.**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/10099?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.08.03_Schiff-Ten_B3_F1_S2_C2_180AC-360DON-RS-T1&t=4&akid=2756%2E259176%2EjEUbGv) | [DONATE >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/10099?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.08.03_Schiff-Ten_B3_F1_S2_C2_180AC-360DON-RS-T1&t=5&akid=2756%2E259176%2EjEUbGv)
---
On the Senate floor, I laid out **ten ways Donald Trump is wrecking this country.** Every American should know that Trump is failing us by:
**10\. Undermining American innovation:** Trump is attacking our world-class research institutions and shutting out international talent, limiting our leadership in science, technology, and medicine.
**9\. Slashing food assistance:** He’s gutting the supplemental nutrition programs that keep millions of American families healthy and ensure our kids don’t go to bed hungry.
**8\. Abandoning our allies:** Trump is weakening our international partnerships, cozying up with dictators, and making America less safe.
**7\. Sabotaging renewable energy:** He’s killing clean energy projects, ceding global renewable energy leadership to China, raising utility bills, and making us more dependent on fossil fuels.
**6\. Damaging public health:** He’s slashing funding for the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and key research programs, meaning cures will be delayed, clinical trials will end, and life-saving care will be harder to access.
**5\. Crippling essential services with DOGE cuts:** From Social Security to wildfire response to public education, Trump is making major funding cuts without worrying about the impact on families, seniors, and kids across the country who will be hurt.
**4\. Tanking the economy with tariffs:** His trade wars are driving up the costs of everyday goods like clothes and groceries while alienating our allies.
**3\. Stripping away healthcare:** Under Trump’s new budget, millions of Americans will lose healthcare coverage. Many rural clinics and hospitals will be forced to close, and all of our healthcare costs will go up.
**2\. Undermining the rule of law:** Trump has been treating the Department of Justice (DOJ) as his own personal political weapon, using it to shield his allies and target his enemies.
**1\. Threatening the very idea of America:** He’s eroding the values that built this country: self-governance, equality, and the belief that no one is above the law — not even the president.
I know this is a lot. And overcoming it will be hard when they control everything. But we will take back the government and put an end to this madness.

I grew up working on the farm in Nash County, every summer until I went to college. Those years taught me firsthand what farming means to this state -- not just as a livelihood, but as the foundation of our rural communities.
Local farms put safe, healthy food on tables across every corner of North Carolina. They drive our state's economy and help supply food banks that serve families in underprivileged communities. Local farmers keep North Carolina moving forward.
But right now, that legacy is being threatened. The federal government's chaotic, erratic tariffs are driving up the costs of equipment, machinery, fertilizer and other essentials that farms depend on. Across the state, I've heard from farmers who are being forced to scale back what they grow. And some are even considering taking a season off from planting altogether.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/1c48dc82-9367-4104-bdee-e5eb510e0754?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Earlier this year, I sat down with Pender, a fourth-generation farmer in Wilson County. His family has endured decades of change, but he told me this moment feels different. With rising inflation, high fuel prices and the added strain of new tariffs, keeping his farm running has never been harder. And Pender's story isn't unique: farmers across North Carolina are facing the same uphill battle.
You can listen to Pender's story here.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4fdd661b-2e67-4a0b-a98b-31b1e99e14be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Agriculture is the number one driver of our economy in North Carolina and our farmers are the backbone. Just last week, I spoke with North Carolina farmers and rural leaders on how we can best support our farms across the state.
I'm running for the U.S. Senate to make sure that our farmers have someone in Washington who understands their challenges and will fight for them.
If you're ready to join me, thank you for [chipping in](https://substack.com/redirect/1c48dc82-9367-4104-bdee-e5eb510e0754?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a few dollars when you can, [registering ](https://substack.com/redirect/59686038-2f6d-4eb2-ba1b-fae8f2680e77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)to vote, or [volunteering](https://substack.com/redirect/a483b31e-de99-4069-8932-f98ed1cd58c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to knock on doors. All of it matters.
