subject: 47th. Out of 50.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Garrity for PA * 4075 Linglestown Rd PMB 119 * Harrisburg, PA 17112-1020 * USA
body:
Pennsylvania just dropped NINE spots in the national rankings. Shapiro says his work is "paying off."

| | | | | [|
---](https://garrityforpa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0c81ef925feae581b13b85deb&id=5e5a111f20&e=63ab67bb25)
| | | | | | Peter,

For nearly a year, I’ve been traveling across this Commonwealth telling you that Pennsylvania is falling behind.
In nearly every speech I’ve given, I’ve cited the same numbers: 38th economically, 39th in education, 41st overall.
Last week, we found out it’s getting worse.
[**According to U.S. News & World Report, Pennsylvania’s economy now ranks 47th out of 50 states in the nation. That’s a drop of 9 spots.**](https://garrityforpa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0c81ef925feae581b13b85deb&id=5b598c903b&e=63ab67bb25)
47th. Out of 50. Only three states in America have a worse-performing economy than ours right now.
And what does Josh Shapiro say? He says his work is “paying off.”
**Paying off for who?**
Not for the families struggling to make ends meet. Not for the small business owners drowning in taxes. Not for the parents watching their kids fall behind in schools that aren’t working.
**Here are the facts:**
📉 Pennsylvania’s economy has dropped from 38th to 47th in the nation under Shapiro
📚 Nearly 7 in 10 eighth graders can’t read at grade level — yet Shapiro refuses to opt into a federal scholarship program that even liberal governors in New York and Colorado have embraced
🌉 Nearly 3,000 bridges across the Commonwealth are structurally deficient — our infrastructure earns a C-minus grade
💸 Pennsylvania has the 5th highest tax burden in the entire country, making it harder to raise a family, start a business, and build a life here
Josh Shapiro talks a lot about one bridge his administration repaired in Philadelphia. One bridge. Meanwhile, thousands of bridges across this state are crumbling, our kids can’t read, and our economy is in free-fall.
That’s not leadership. That’s a press release.
But here’s the good news:
**It doesn’t have to be this way.**
As Governor, I won’t just talk about Pennsylvania’s problems. I have a plan to solve them.
🏡 **Deliver meaningful property tax relief** so seniors can stay in the homes they spent a lifetime building.
⚡ **Lower electric and utility bills** by unleashing Pennsylvania energy, eliminating unnecessary taxes on utilities, and ending costly government mandates.
💰 **Reduce insurance costs** by cutting red tape, increasing competition, and cracking down on fraud.
💊 **Lower prescription drug costs** by taking on the middlemen driving up prices and strengthening programs that help seniors afford the medications they need.
❤️ **Support family caregivers** so more Pennsylvanians can age at home with dignity and independence.
📉 **Restore fiscal discipline** in Harrisburg so today's overspending doesn't become tomorrow's tax increase.
That’s what a turnaround looks like.
Not more speeches.
Not more photo ops.
Not more excuses.
Real solutions that make Pennsylvania more affordable, more competitive, and a place where our children choose to stay instead of feeling like they need to leave.
47th is not who we are.
And it certainly isn’t where we’re going.
With your help, we’re going to turn Pennsylvania around.
Onward,

Just a reminder, Team: Earlier this year the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act of 1965 — one of the most consequential policies in American history — with the case Louisiana v. Callais .
The ruling makes it nearly impossible to challenge district maps that dilute the power of underrepresented communities. Representatives can now choose their voters instead of the other way around.
What happened in the aftermath? Hours after the decision, Florida lawmakers passed a new congressional map designed to flip four U.S. House seats. States across the South began redrawing their maps, even in states where voters had already cast their ballots in primaries.
The Supreme Court didn't just fail to protect your vote. The Court’s Trump-appointed or MAGA-aligned majority actively dismantled the protections designed to make it count.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Let me tell you a story about how and why I got started in politics.
body:
I didn’t plan to run for governor. But Greg Abbott left me no choice.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter, it's Gina. I’ll be completely honest with you:
**I never planned on running for Governor.** I never planned on being in politics at all.
But after a decade of Greg Abbott abandoning our schools, families, and communities, it’s obvious: If we want change, we have to create it ourselves.
Peter, I’d like to tell you more about my story and why I’m running. [**But if you’re ready to take action now, you can chip in here to power our fight for Texas.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260804_2_politics.IQuGhL&refcode=em20260804-1743&amount=5&t=1&akid=1743%2E299639%2Eu_T9ss)
I loved my work as a civil rights and union lawyer. I fought every day for families, workers, and fairness. I represented Texans who had been pushed around or shut out, people who just wanted what they had earned: fair well-paying jobs, dignity, and a chance to build a better life. I thought I’d do that work forever.
**But sometimes life puts a decision in front of you that you can’t ignore.**
For me, that moment came the day I learned my son’s elementary school was being closed because of budget cuts. It wasn’t failing or unsafe — just “in the way” of a plan to hand schools over to private interests looking to profit off our kids' futures. Families and teachers were shaken and uncertain of what would come next, and I realized something terrifying: **No one was coming to save us.**
So I stepped up. I ran for the Austin ISD’s Board of Trustees, won, and helped block a corporate takeover of our public schools.
It taught me something powerful: **When Texans stand up, we win big battles.**
But the fight was just starting. Neighborhood schools kept closing across Texas because Republican leaders kept diverting money away from classrooms. So I made another decision I never expected to make: I ran for the Texas House.
As a state representative, I secured billions in school funding. I passed a first-of-its-kind law so Texas businesses could do well financially and do good in our communities. I delivered nearly a billion dollars in healthcare funding to Travis County. I helped organize walkouts that blocked Abbott’s voter suppression bill and fought back against his school voucher scheme.
**The same determination I’ve had my entire career is why I’m running for Governor of Texas today — to defend the Texas I grew up with and fight for every family who calls this state home.**
**Because Texas simply can’t afford another four years of Greg Abbott.**
For a decade, Abbot has sold out working families to enrich the wealthy and powerful at every step. He kicks children off Medicaid to save a few extra bucks for Big Pharma. He shuts down public schools so private interests can get rich on vouchers. He ignores families crushed by rising prices while he funnels nearly a billion of our taxpayer dollars into no-bid contracts for his donors.
With your help, I can become the next Governor of Texas. I’ve beaten Abbott before, and I’m ready to do it again. And right now, _he’s the least popular he’s ever been_ — so this is our chance.
But defeating a three-term incumbent backed by right-wing billionaire money takes real people power. It takes Texans standing up together and saying: Enough.
So I’m asking you directly, Peter: **[Can I count on you to pitch in $5 today and power the movement to take Texas back?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260804_2_politics.IQuGhL&refcode=em20260804-1743&amount=5&t=2&akid=1743%2E299639%2Eu_T9ss)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260804_2_politics.IQuGhL&amount=5&refcode=em20260804-1743&t=21&akid=1743%2E299639%2Eu_T9ss)
With gratitude,
Gina Hinojosa

---
Peter,
The New York Times ran a piece asking a question that would have sounded impossible two years ago: **is this the year Florida turns blue?**
They watched us flip the Miami mayor's office, a long-shot State Senate seat, and even the State House district that covers Mar-a-Lago. And they came away taking David's campaign seriously, because they see what we see: **Florida is ready for a new direction.**
**[When the national press starts paying attention, so do our opponents. So we have to ask: will you chip in $10 between our campaign and Blue Amp Action right now to keep this momentum going?](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13934?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.08.04_Jolly-Polling_B2_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=5&akid=2787%2E259176%2EAYjVa4)**
Here's what David has been saying on the road. _We’re winning._
We know how that sounds in a state that hasn't elected a Democratic Governor in a generation. But David has been in every corner of Florida, and what he's hearing is that people are exhausted. They're tired of the culture wars, the toxicity, and leaders who pick fights instead of solving problems.
What they want is someone laser-focused on the cost of housing, health care, and electricity. They want someone who focus on the things that unite us, and on tackling the issues we all face together.
Here's the catch, and the Times printed this too. Our opponent Byron Donalds has raised a massive warchest, and it’s only August.
The GOP is ready to pour hundreds of millions of dollars into this race, bankrolled by the special interests that have run Tallahassee for thirty years. They'll spend whatever it takes to ensure they hold on to power.
We are not going to match them dollar for dollar. We don't have to.
**What we have to do is the work, neighbor to neighbor, conversation by conversation, all across this state. That's how we built this moment, and that's how we protect it.**
**[So we're asking: can you split a donation today to keep this moving?](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13934?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.08.04_Jolly-Polling_B2_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=6&akid=2787%2E259176%2EAYjVa4)**

We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates, If you'd like to unsubscribe, “Is this the year Florida turns blue?” \- The New York Times, 6/23/26 | Peter, The New York Times ran a piece asking a question that would have sounded impossible two years ago: is this the year Florida turns blue? They watched us flip the Miami mayor's office, a long-shot State Senate seat, and even the State House district that covers Mar-a-Lago. And they came away taking David's campaign seriously, because they see what we see: Florida is ready for a new direction. Here's what David has been saying on the road. We’re winning. We know how that sounds in a state that hasn't elected a Democratic Governor in a generation. But David has been in every corner of Florida, and what he's hearing is that people are exhausted. They're tired of the culture wars, the toxicity, and leaders who pick fights instead of solving problems. What they want is someone laser-focused on the cost of housing, health care, and electricity. They want someone who focus on the things that unite us, and on tackling the issues we all face together. Here's the catch, and the Times printed this too. Our opponent Byron Donalds has raised a massive warchest, and it’s only August. The GOP is ready to pour hundreds of millions of dollars into this race, bankrolled by the special interests that have run Tallahassee for thirty years. They'll spend whatever it takes to ensure they hold on to power. We are not going to match them dollar for dollar. We don't have to. What we have to do is the work, neighbor to neighbor, conversation by conversation, all across this state. That's how we built this moment, and that's how we protect it. body:
Not what I spent my time doing

| | | | | |
Peter,
I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. I couldn't just sit there.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDgwNF9JTi0xUC4xMTAxMTdfdDE5Nzg5MzgtMjA2OCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA4MDRfSU4tMVAuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTc4OTM4LTIwNjgifQ/GKQsOWjPmb4nwpmeX3NPrw)
But here is the hard truth: fighting the radical Left and standing up for our values is incredibly expensive. I don’t have a massive machine behind me. I don’t have someone who can write blank checks on a whim.
[I just have normal folks like you.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDgwNF9JTi0xUC4xMTAxMTdfdDE5Nzg5MzgtMjA2OCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA4MDRfSU4tMVAuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTc4OTM4LTIwNjgifQ/LRKhP7S8aUCzNsJswSNziA)

They said defeating Speaker Mike Johnson is going to take a helluva lot of hard work. Well, here’s the good news: I'm no stranger to hard work — I've got the dirt on my overalls to prove it. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-conrad]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/120031/images/Screen%20Shot%202026-08-04%20at%2010.14.00%20AM.png]
My name is Conrad Cable, and I'm the Democrat running against Mike Johnson.
I'm a farmer. My overalls have dirt on them because I put it there, working my own land. My hands are rough. And I've never once been scared of hard work — I was raised to believe that if you want something to grow, you show up and you put the work in, every single day, rain or shine, no excuses.
Mike Johnson has never worked a day like that in his life.
He's spent his career in courtrooms and committee rooms, cutting deals for people who've never set foot on a farm in this district, let alone broken a sweat on one. And now, as Speaker of the House, he's used that power to gut Medicaid and turn a blind eye while a private company tortures our neighbors at Winn Correction Center.
I'm a 6th-generation Louisianian. This is my home. And I grew up believing that the people who work the hardest and ask for the least are exactly the people who deserve to be fought for. That's not a talking point to me — that's just how I was raised. Mike Johnson wouldn't know honest, hard work if it walked up and shook his hand.
I'm running because this district — our farms, our families, our neighbors — deserves a fighter who isn't afraid to get dirty for them. Not someone who answers to Washington donors and corporate PACs. Someone who answers to you.
I know Mike Johnson and the powerful interests behind him are going to spend whatever it takes to keep this seat. They always do. But there are things money can't buy: the sweat you put into your own land, the loyalty you have to your neighbors, and the truth about who's actually willing to work for you.
Will you chip in $25, $10, or whatever you can to help me take on Mike Johnson and start building the kind of campaign this district has never seen? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-conrad]
DONATE TODAY TO DEFEAT SPEAKER MIKE JOHNSON! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-conrad]
Thank you for standing with me.
Conrad Cable
Democrat for Louisiana’s 4th

Peter,
The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has one job: helping Americans prepare for and recover from disasters.
But the Trump administration is pushing the agency into a dangerous new role—funding efforts aimed at what it calls “organized political violence,” even before a crime has occurred.
At a time when hurricanes, floods, and wildfires are devastating communities across the country, every FEMA dollar should be strengthening emergency preparedness and helping families rebuild—not expanding political surveillance.
FEMA was created as a civil agency. It must remain focused on saving lives, delivering relief, and ensuring that every family receives help after a disaster.

A social media investigator is raising questions about the conditions placed on a Sam Altman-linked data center project, pointing to noise limits as a key regulatory constraint.
In a TikTok video posted June 4, Hunter Carrithers--known online as [@digitaloilhunter](https://substack.com/redirect/1d98f0ba-0114-40db-a037-a1e369670687?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--highlighted documentation indicating that a data center associated with the OpenAI chief executive "may not exceed historical decibel levels." Carrithers, who describes himself as working "inside the refinery" of the digital economy, appended a call for additional evidence to the post, writing: "files Please upload details."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e56e7601-b701-4a9b-82c8-10c04ce396e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The video enters a crowded conversation surrounding the infrastructure powering the artificial intelligence boom. Carrithers has built a following documenting the often-hidden costs of data center construction, including the strain on electrical grids and local communities. Previous posts have cited figures including 12,600 miles of new transmission lines and $60 billion in grid upgrades to support over 400 Texas data centers, with warnings of potential electricity cost spikes for consumers.
The noise restriction referenced in the latest video reflects an increasingly common battleground in AI facility siting. As server farms expand to accommodate power-hungry AI workloads, their cooling systems and backup generators have drawn noise complaints from neighboring residents and businesses. Municipalities across the country are now imposing strict acoustic limits on new data center projects--a trend that can significantly constrain where and how these facilities operate.
[Share Heartland Journal ®](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1zdWJzdGFjayZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PXNoYXJlJmFjdGlvbj1zaGFyZSIsInAiOjIwOTgyNjg4MiwicyI6NjcyOTU4OSwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc4NTg2OTI1MywiZXhwIjoyMTAxNDQ1MjUzLCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.4c8Wseq0E-hqjVeyoYjx8YnN7LzixcuTDx9sgjArxyU?)
Carrithers' reporting style blends on-the-ground technical analysis with crowdsourced verification. His request for viewers to upload supporting files suggests the decibel-level restriction may have surfaced through preliminary public records, with the creator seeking community assistance to build out the full documentation.
The video also gestures toward broader labor and ethical concerns within the industry. Earlier this year, Carrithers featured an electrician who stated he would rather quit than participate in data center construction--a signal that opposition to the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure is coming from multiple directions, including the workforce tasked with erecting it.
OpenAI and Altman have not publicly responded to the specific claims raised in the video. However, the company is known to be aggressively pursuing data center partnerships and compute capacity to train and run its large language models.
Whether the noise restriction proves to be a routine zoning condition or a meaningful obstacle to operations remains to be seen. For now, Carrithers' reporting adds another data point to the growing scrutiny over who bears the costs--and the decibels--of the AI expansion.

* **[Host a yard sign](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/SZYNzYS8ujvS3XnwWYQ5BA~~/AAUS1hA~/5pWVGLD1rvOBvt6mHZqfUWqr5AKYl4XjL-lZv39gvd_Je9dUpNYNp8AecGeXMBukkNsX1KCtHRVvxkcxtB6MkB1aCzMjj37g6CLl4K6F_f-EqQ3d8izg5o2uGumP8h_h)** _(we’ve got 1,500 out in the field, and we’re looking to plant 600 more by August 15th!)_

With our primary election next month, every door knocked, phone call made, and sign planted matters more than ever. That’s why we’re asking, whether or not you can donate, if you’ll join our volunteer team today. You can volunteer from anywhere! As the years went on, the trauma only grew deeper. To survive, she turned to addiction \- the only way to numb the pain. The only way to keep going. She even had children with one of the men who trafficked her. Another chain and reason it felt impossible to escape. For years, she lived in fear. No way out. Until one day, she reached a breaking point. With nothing but courage and fear in her heart, she ran, fleeing to a women's shelter. No plan. No safety.
**Just hope that maybe someone would help her. ** **And that is when everything began to change. ****Because someone did show up. **A partner of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** called House Parent Project. They didn't turn her away. They didn't question her worth. **They sat with her, they listened and believed her. And in that moment, light entered her story. **

They helped her take the next step.Then the next. And the next. They safely relocated her far from the people who had controlled her life. **For the first time in years, she could breathe.** She could begin to heal. But they didn't stop there. They are still walking with her today, because her fight is not over. Her children are still connected to the man who trafficked her. And now, Sara is fighting to bring them to safety. Fighting to break the cycle for good. And she is not alone.

Friend, maybe this is your first time hearing about us. The **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists for one reason: **_To stop the sale of God 's children._** We were born from the true story told in the film _Sound of Freedom, _but this mission did not end when the credits rolled. It became a movement. Today, we work around the world to **prevent trafficking before it starts. ****We support partners that help rescue children in danger, support survivors on their long road to healing, and fight for laws that protect the innocent.**

clean_body: A child cried out... someone answered| | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | Friend,She was just a child. And the person who should have protected her was the one who first trafficked her. Her own mother. What began there didn't stop. She was sold again and again. Passed between people who saw her as an object. Not a child. Not a life. Not someone worth protecting. As the years went on, the trauma only grew deeper. To survive, she turned to addiction \- the only way to numb the pain. The only way to keep going. She even had children with one of the men who trafficked her. Another chain and reason it felt impossible to escape. For years, she lived in fear. No way out. Until one day, she reached a breaking point. With nothing but courage and fear in her heart, she ran, fleeing to a women's shelter. No plan. No safety. Just hope that maybe someone would help her. And that is when everything began to change. Because someone did show up. A partner of the Sound of Freedom Foundation called House Parent Project. They didn't turn her away. They didn't question her worth. They sat with her, they listened and believed her. And in that moment, light entered her story. They helped her take the next step.Then the next. And the next. They safely relocated her far from the people who had controlled her life. For the first time in years, she could breathe. She could begin to heal. But they didn't stop there. They are still walking with her today, because her fight is not over. Her children are still connected to the man who trafficked her. And now, Sara is fighting to bring them to safety. Fighting to break the cycle for good. And she is not alone. Friend, maybe this is your first time hearing about us. The Sound of Freedom Foundation exists for one reason: To stop the sale of God 's children. We were born from the true story told in the film Sound of Freedom, but this mission did not end when the credits rolled. It became a movement. Today, we work around the world to prevent trafficking before it starts. We support partners that help rescue children in danger, support survivors on their long road to healing, and fight for laws that protect the innocent. Because rescue is only the beginning. Children need safety, healing and someone to walk with them on the long road ahead. And that is what your support makes possible. Not just escape. But restoration. A future rebuilt. You see, Friend, Sound of Freedom Foundation 's mission is simple: To stop the sale of God 's children. We extend the reach of the Sound of Freedom film, shining a light on how real and widespread child trafficking is and what we must do to stop it. We believe in a future where this evil is gone. A world where every child is safe and truly free. Jesus said, " Whoever welcomes one little child like this in my name welcomes me." (Matthew 18:5) Today you have the chance to be part of that welcome and be part of that light. Your gift today can help: $25 -- Support immediate outreach and response $50 -- Provide critical care and stabilization $75 -- Help relocate and protect a survivor $100 -- Support ongoing care and legal advocacy Because healing takes time. Protection takes people. And freedom takes courage from all of us. You can step in and help rewrite stories like Sara's. Please give as generously as you can today. And please pray... For Sara. For her children. And for every child still waiting for someone to show up. Because God 's children are not for sale. And together... we will not stop fighting for them. For God's Children, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074

Two measures. Two opposite answers. One Colorado income tax rate.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Polis signed a $99.6M insurance fee enterprise kept [just under the threshold requiring a Prop 117 vote](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Victor Marx named [Col. George Markert his running mate](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in the three-way governor's race with Weiser and Lopez. Federal judges [rebuked a Colorado immigration judge](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over detainee bond rulings. A [Denver street takeover drew no arrests](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) despite police calling it "incredibly dangerous." Sterling Ranch welcomed John Adams Academy, [a new Founders-focused charter school](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Colorado voters may face [dueling tax measures](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.): a graduated income tax raising ~$2B, or a constitutional 4.4% rate cap.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Stephen Moore told ALEC that [data-center misinformation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) is fueling opposition, calling the buildout vital to beating China in AI. Columnist Brian Joondeph questions [whether Trump's "America First" pledge is holding up](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) five months into the Iran conflict.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Cory Gaines flags a projected 16,000-student enrollment drop — the first sustained decline in 30 years — urging voters to [understand school funding before a TABOR-refund ballot measure](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Pastor Drake Hunter recalls drifting unnoticed off Cozumel, [a parable for drifting from faith](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), per Matthew 6:33. And Logan McCahill reports 1 in 10 Coloradans now use SNAP, with the state set to pay a share of benefits starting October 2027 — [an estimated $180-$210 million a year](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, August 4, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Two measures. Two opposite answers. One Colorado income tax rate.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Colorado voters may face a choice in November between two measures that couldn’t disagree more about the state income tax. One would replace the flat rate with a graduated system and raise close to $2 billion a year. The other would make it illegal to raise the rate at all.
Neither one is a new idea. And the differences between them go deeper than the rate.
Colorado’s income tax has been flat since 1987, meaning everyone pays the same percentage regardless of what they earn. The rate is currently 4.40 percent.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado’s new insurance fee enterprise can lower or stop collecting to stay under Proposition 117](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Colorado Democrats structured a new insurance fee just under the voter-approval threshold, projected to land within $400,000 of the cap that would have required a public vote._
* **A fee engineered to skip voters:** Gov. Jared Polis signed SB26-155, creating the Strengthen Colorado Homes Enterprise, with a Legislative Council fiscal note projecting exactly $99.6 million in collections over five years — just under the $100 million threshold that Proposition 117 requires voters to approve.
* **The rate drops as premiums rise:** The 0.5 percent fee charged to insurers is set to be cut by more than half, to 0.24 percent, after year one, even as the state's own projections show homeowner premiums growing every year — a built-in reduction the law explicitly allows to keep total revenue under the cap.
* **Part of a broader pattern, per watchdog data:** The Common Sense Institute found this is one of ten Colorado enterprises created since Proposition 117 took effect that avoided a voter referral, as fee-enterprise revenue statewide has grown from $225 to $4,692 per resident since 2000 — now exceeding half the entire state budget.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 2** _We’ve spent a lot of time with nursery rhymes lately. Today, let’s trade Mother Goose for a swimsuit. Have you ever done something wonderfully weird? Nearly 14 years ago, while celebrating our twenty-fifth wedding anniversary, Sherrie and I traveled to Cozumel, Mexico. One morning we signed up for a snorkeling excursion in the beautiful Caribbean Sea._ __
**[Convention of States has a Colorado bill ready for 2027. It still has no sponsor.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | JULY 30** _Convention of States Action (COSA) says more than 62,000 Coloradans have signed its petitions calling for a constitutional convention to impose fiscal restraints on the federal government, limit its power, and set term limits for Congress. The organization has a draft bill ready for the 2027 legislative session._
**[History, when convenient: Colorado media’s selective celebration of representation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | JULY 30**
_On July 28, Colorado election officials confirmed that Greg Lopez and Taralyn Romero had qualified for the November general election ballot as unaffiliated candidates for governor and lieutenant governor. Their campaign submitted 11,948 valid signatures, exceeding the requirement in every congressional district._

| I'll admit it:
I never thought I'd see the day when I'd say someone is making Randy Fine look reasonable.
But here we are. For years, Dan Bilzerian built his public image around controversy. Guns. Gambling. Misogyny. Conspiracy theories. Whatever would generate the next viral headline.
---
| [](https://eboq88hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001SFJO3LX0Rv2mxiN9jb4pjRebKHw7WtDHTkolKSAxV8N9xBEVHJDE68W0SSS56M6bNeTYH2pe3ecM58ePgoUe5vvi4aRZ6jLXJRpbVBpGIiOPRcwZteb8A8DcXBxNa3wKIq4CbbV5sn2z595aAmKHu0YzTcBpneziVpak3zmJCBItiMJ35P5NuaCib_oCpWKsV9sVmHEDPU0TGgaCnY6-4BN8CzNaEN7QaE7hRJ5RYGrplwPqNHk2SQ==&c=Fqw6o13SH_Ol_QyQJ-c_5JiBmcig_4rUVVVXoYvxtI_UP6Szq0EoGw==&ch=MfRFE8Z8Wik5BiFYU8G5psGJ91xr-1jEjE7PLCyykybAgYL78qNOjA==)
---
Now he's gone even further.
Bilzerian has drawn widespread condemnation for antisemitic rhetoric, Holocaust-related remarks, and repeated attacks on Jewish people.
Instead of walking those comments back, he's leaned into them--turning hate into a political strategy designed to grab attention and divide people.
That's not leadership.
It's not courage.
And it has no place in Congress.
I've disagreed with Randy Fine on just about everything. But Bilzerian's embrace of antisemitic rhetoric crosses a line that should be unacceptable to every American, regardless of party.
This race is about more than one candidate.
It's about whether we allow people to build political movements around outrage, conspiracy theories, and bigotry--or whether we stand up and say enough is enough. I believe our community deserves a representative who fights for affordable housing, good-paying jobs, safer neighborhoods, and opportunity for everyone--not someone chasing internet fame by spreading hatred.
But I can't win this race alone.
Dan Bilzerian has a massive platform, wealthy supporters, and millions of people who know his name. We're building something different: a grassroots campaign powered by people who believe decency still matters.
My name is Ronnie Murchinson-Rivera. I'm a Democrat, Father, law enforcement and EMS professional, and I'm running because I believe Congress needs fewer extremists and more public servants.
[If you agree, will you chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can today? Every contribution helps us reach more voters and prove that integrity can still beat outrage.](https://eboq88hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001SFJO3LX0Rv2mxiN9jb4pjRebKHw7WtDHTkolKSAxV8N9xBEVHJDE68W0SSS56M6bNeTYH2pe3ecM58ePgoUe5vvi4aRZ6jLXJRpbVBpGIiOPRcwZteb8A8DcXBxNa3wKIq4CbbV5sn2z595aAmKHu0YzTcBpneziVpak3zmJCBItiMJ35P5NuaCib_oCpWKsV9sVmHEDPU0TGgaCnY6-4BN8CzNaEN7Qz4QWBusqjWmeiyDIBOzF3Q==&c=Fqw6o13SH_Ol_QyQJ-c_5JiBmcig_4rUVVVXoYvxtI_UP6Szq0EoGw==&ch=MfRFE8Z8Wik5BiFYU8G5psGJ91xr-1jEjE7PLCyykybAgYL78qNOjA==)

Right now, Senate Republicans are signing off on a bogus deal to give Trump’s personal lawyer total control of the DOJ. Before I dive in, will you pitch in to help EON take on this corruption head-on? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?amount=25]
Back in January, Donald Trump filed a $10 billion sham lawsuit against the IRS for disclosing tax returns from his first term.
Then in May, he dropped the suit in exchange for the creation of a $1.8 billion fund to compensate his allies who claim they were wrongfully targeted by the Biden administration — AKA January 6 rioters.
That settlement also banned the IRS from auditing Trump's tax returns, his son’s tax returns, his company, and any of his affiliated trusts. Peter,
While all eyes are on the outcome of today's Democratic Senate primary in Michigan, there is something insidious happening in the state.
This morning, the Trump Justice Department deployed federal election monitors to four Michigan cities. Detroit. Hamtramck. Lansing. East Lansing. Every one of them Democratic-leaning. Between them they hold some of the largest Black, Arab American, and college student populations in the state.
Not one Republican stronghold is on the list:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DcZ_9uXRrbv2r74jxgelFyow0UCgFZ_E6iNkmKROuY4qO9wsDggdJeWIW9GrwN-12O_MnsEQfY7aFyrvwqQFnVpgMY-w1DWvREkYFLhblRdFuy17b6MpeWGsw64RLc69f_nMIW74VPyUdCLxiXX8czCPecI33rsN2r1aMQ4HpmNuQke18a_yMB4r4o61x1wR-6HO11bzpw1Bhc7knfAVtdTfEFdvEHrS69FOlf9lLVA=&c=NtDO6rqX6Q5hXeLUGN5bLxWswWF4FynwQevbMbWmEqWrJZgyzVSf5w==&ch=vkX-jVcd3fEfyngLV6eBIovVb6tWVttjouZDSqj3HLIYzjwukZ2m7Q==)

The Trump administration is quietly using today's Michigan primary as a dry run for their election rigging scheme. They are not looking for fraud. There is no rampant voter fraud to find, and there never was. So what is the point?
Today's primary in Michigan is where the administration is gathering information and testing the bounds. Which clerks push back. How fast a city responds to a federal document demand. What a monitor presence does to turnout in a majority-Muslim precinct or a campus ward.
Trump is practicing his assault on free and fair elections at this very moment. If Democrats are going to flip the House and Senate this November, we need to make this election too big to rig. And we need courts strong enough to hold the line against Trump's attacks on our elections.
That's why what Defend Our Courts is doing matters so much at this moment. We're fighting to expand the firewall of state Supreme Courts on a national scale this November and turning out voters in states with key House and Senate races. But to operate at the scale this moment demands, we need your help--right now.

_Peter, this is Mazie. Below is a message from Troy Jackson, who is running for Senate in Maine. Please read his message below._
* * *
Peter, I grew up in a working-class family in Allagash. We didn’t always have heat or running water. Sometimes, we relied on food assistance to make ends meet. My dad was a logger out in the woods, and one day he and his fellow loggers had to stand up to a wealthy landowner who was threatening their wages. They weren’t even asking for more money, they just wanted to be paid fairly. _“Take the pay cut or go home,”_ they were told. I’ll never forget that day. I was only 11 years old, and watched my dad fight for something bigger than all of us — a basic fairness every worker should be entitled to, the ability to make ends meet, the ability to put food on the table for their family. I know what it’s like to worry about paying the bills on time. I know what it’s like to fight, not just for your own future, but for the future of everyone around you, too. And it’s _that fight_ I’ll bring to the United States Senate. For too long, our voices have been ignored and crushed by powerful corporations and special interests who make backroom deals with greedy politicians. Now’s our chance to change that. Peter, we have less than 100 days to build a campaign big enough to defeat Susan Collins. But with your help today, I know we can do it. I promise you I’ll spend every day in the Senate fighting for you and your families. **[So that’s why I have to ask: can you chip in a donation of any amount split between my campaign and Mazie Hirono to defeat Collins and take back our Democratic majority?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136626717/638053245/-554660266?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260804_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZTRiM2E2NS0zODkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VE_s_7ULcTAXG3LTv5FB4lMiQ8gTe7r6qHIkuwe6Tb4=)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Troy Jackson and Mazie Hirono will go through immediately:_ **** | | **[CHIP IN $10 NOW](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136626718/638053246/-554660266?express_lane=true&amount=10&refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260804_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZTRiM2E2NS0zODkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VE_s_7ULcTAXG3LTv5FB4lMiQ8gTe7r6qHIkuwe6Tb4=)**

clean_body: | Peter, this is Mazie. Below is a message from Troy Jackson, who is running for Senate in Maine. Please read his message below. Peter, I grew up in a working-class family in Allagash. We didn’t always have heat or running water. Sometimes, we relied on food assistance to make ends meet. My dad was a logger out in the woods, and one day he and his fellow loggers had to stand up to a wealthy landowner who was threatening their wages. They weren’t even asking for more money, they just wanted to be paid fairly. “Take the pay cut or go home,” they were told. I’ll never forget that day. I was only 11 years old, and watched my dad fight for something bigger than all of us — a basic fairness every worker should be entitled to, the ability to make ends meet, the ability to put food on the table for their family. I know what it’s like to worry about paying the bills on time. I know what it’s like to fight, not just for your own future, but for the future of everyone around you, too. And it’s that fight I’ll bring to the United States Senate. For too long, our voices have been ignored and crushed by powerful corporations and special interests who make backroom deals with greedy politicians. Now’s our chance to change that. Peter, we have less than 100 days to build a campaign big enough to defeat Susan Collins. But with your help today, I know we can do it. I promise you I’ll spend every day in the Senate fighting for you and your families. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Troy Jackson and Mazie Hirono will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = I appreciate your support always, Troy = Friends of Mazie Hirono 335 Merchant Street #677 Honolulu, HI 96809 United States mailto:info@mazieforhawaii.com | Paid for by Mazie Hirono For Hawaii

An important step forward... | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5858288?e=6736d7bc47)
---
| | [ ](https://andyfornevada.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6816f620b82a1d3ac2a6c980d&id=4a9614284e&e=6736d7bc47)
---
| | Dear Peter,

Big news, my friend. Yesterday, I officially filed my request with the Nevada Legislature to bring my Inspector General bill forward during the upcoming 2027 Legislative Session.

As you’ll probably recall, in 2025 I introduced a bill to create an Office of Inspector General, with the authority to audit any entity that receives state funding, to ensure your hard-earned tax dollars aren’t being wasted. My bill received a hearing, but the Democrats in control of the Legislature refused to schedule it for a vote.

Of course, the case for this bill has only grown stronger since then. Nevada is one of the few states in the country without an Inspector General, and the massive fraud scandal that rocked Minnesota (which also lacks such a position) a few months ago served as a reminder of why it’s critical to have proper oversight of government finances.

That’s why I’m bringing this important bill back.

And it’s why it’s so critical that I’m re-elected as Nevada Controller this November — so that I’m still here to advocate for this bill and fight for the transparency and accountability you deserve!

To that end, I hope you’ll consider [a contribution to my campaign](https://andyfornevada.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6816f620b82a1d3ac2a6c980d&id=263934d6a4&e=6736d7bc47) today, so that I’ll have the resources necessary to get my message out to voters all across our state.

We know the Democrats are going to do all they can to take me out this year — as they showed in their refusal to vote on my Inspector General bill last year, they don’t want the kind of government accountability I’m pushing for.

We can’t let them succeed. And your contribution today will help make sure they don’t.

[You can contribute by clicking here](https://andyfornevada.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6816f620b82a1d3ac2a6c980d&id=cc3bdb6fee&e=6736d7bc47).

Thank you for your consideration, and I hope you have a great week!

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

clean_body: PRIMARY TURNOUT REPORT 📎| | | Dear friend, I wanted to reach out to you personally and share what’s keeping me up at night. Enthusiasm among Republicans is down and the data proves it. Just look at this voter turnout chart from North Carolina’s March primary. Democrats showed up in full force—blowing Republicans out of the water. And to make matters worse, unaffiliated voters broke heavily for Democrats. According to The Carolina Journal, 55.9% of them chose a Democratic ballot. I haven’t seen Democrats this motivated in years. They don’t have candidates worth rallying around, but they hate President Trump and they’re desperate to derail his agenda. That is what’s driving them, and if they succeed, they’ll put America last. Higher taxes.Liberal indoctrination of our children.Lawless borders. I could go on and on, but I know I don’t have to—you’ve lived through this before. If we don’t hold our majority in Congress, President Trump will be powerless and we could soon feel like we’re back in the Biden era. That’s why I had to reach out to you. I know you have donated in the past and I’d be honored to have your help on this race. In fact, I really need it if we’re going to win. Elections aren’t won on Election Day anymore. They’re won by campaigns that ramp up early and refuse to let the other side outwork them. Please join me today and help us celebrate a victory in November. | | | | | The stakes are too high to sit on the sidelines. I’m all in, and I hope you’ll jump in and help us defend this seat. Sincerely, | | Chuck Edwards | | | | Stay in Touch 👇 Paid for by Edwards for Congress | | | ---|---|---

Team,

July was a busy month for Nellie, in Washington and back home in NJ-09. Here's a look back at what she's been up to:

Cracking down on ticket scams. Nellie introduced the HOLDBACKS Act to stop the practices that leave fans paying much more for concerts and games than they should.

Fighting for our hospitals. Nellie is protecting the healthcare New Jersey families and seniors depend on, and working to keep local hospitals open and fully funded.

Celebrating our Peruvian community. Nellie joined four different Peruvian organizations from across the district to celebrate Peru's independence and NJ-09’s vibrant Peruvian community.

Cleaning up our waterways. Nellie's bipartisan CLEAN-UP Act, which will help protect local waterways, was approved by the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

Investing in Passaic Ave. Nellie announced a major federal investment in the Passaic Avenue corridor to improve safety for pedestrians and cyclists.

None of this happens without a team that shows up, and none of it continues without the resources to keep fighting through November.

What if America's global chaos isn't just bad luck?
One of China's most influential strategists, [Jin Canrong](https://substack.com/redirect/f96af83d-ac5c-45cb-9743-298e6bb3c6d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), laid out a theory that should alarm every American: give the United States multiple enemies, and it will become strategically paralyzed.
> "If America has three enemies outside, I estimate it will begin to become dizzy. If it has four, it will completely lose its direction." ~ Jin Canrong
Look around. Ukraine. Iran. China. North Korea. Cartels. The border. Is this coincidence--or exactly the kind of strategic environment Beijing hoped to create?
In this [piece](https://substack.com/redirect/f96af83d-ac5c-45cb-9743-298e6bb3c6d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), I examine Jin's argument and ask the question Washington refuses to answer: **[Are we walking into China's strategy exactly as planned?](https://substack.com/redirect/f96af83d-ac5c-45cb-9743-298e6bb3c6d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Josh Philips, Epoch Times Senior Investigative Journalist, and I discuss China's intent and hand in distracting America.

subject: They’re afraid of my movement, they always have been.

Peter,
The day we have all worked so hard for is here: the Missouri Primary!
Since I first ran for Congress in 2018, I’ve known I would face hardships. I knew it would be tough, and I’d be up against some fierce opponents who don’t want to see a progressive Black woman in power.
That has all proven to be true.
I also knew that our coalition, our movement, would come together and support one another as it has time and time again. You see, in 2020, I defeated a 52-year political dynasty, and in 2022, St. Louis sent me back to Congress with a strong mandate to champion racial, economic, reproductive, gender, health, and environmental justice. And I did just that.
Then, last cycle, AIPAC spent $25 million to take out Jamaal Bowman and me. It was the most expensive primary campaign a super PAC has ever run against progressives...
Now I’m running to take this seat back. Outside spending has booked more than $4.3 million against me this cycle. They’re afraid of our movement—they always have been.
In these final hours, I need your help. Today is critical. Right-wing billionaires have thrown their weight behind my opponent, Wesley Bell, a former Republican campaign manager who is willing to do Trump and his billionaire friends' bidding at the expense of our communities.
Peter, before the day ends, can you join us in the fight by making a contribution of $10, $20, or $50 today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q3?refcode=x_260804_Coriprimaryday_act]
DONATE BEFORE AUG. 4TH [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q3?refcode=x_260804_Coriprimaryday_act]
We are out and about until the last possible moment tonight, getting folks to the polls, getting our message out, and fighting for every single vote because every conversation, every knock, and every ballot could make the difference.
Regardless of the outcome of this race, I feel so grateful and so blessed to have so many supporters and fighters in this with us. I’m so proud of what we’ve accomplished, and I look forward to the road ahead.
Thank you for being a part of the team. Now, let’s win this! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q3?refcode=x_260804_Coriprimaryday_act]
In solidarity,
Cori Bush

As a Congresswoman, she has always shown up when it’s hardest: securing disaster relief, lowering insulin costs, and delivering millions for our communities.

Wes Climer, the Republican nominee for South Carolina's Fifth Congressional District, will kick off his General Election campaign
next Thursday, August 13, with a rally featuring U.S. Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana.

Wes Climer is running for Congress with a clear conservative vision: secure our border, cut taxes and government spending, protect
parental rights, defend faith and family, restore accountability in Washington, and put America First. He's proven he'll stand up
to the political establishment when it's the right thing to do, and now he's ready to take that same fight to Congress. Winning
this general election is critical to ensuring South Carolina's 5th District has a proven conservative leader who will deliver
results—not just make promises.

Senator Kennedy, known for his plainspoken defense of conservative principles in Washington, will join Climer to discuss fiscal
responsibility, constitutional government, and the stakes of the November election for South Carolina families. Kennedy serves on
the Senate Appropriations, Banking, Budget, and Judiciary Committees.

"Senator Kennedy has never been afraid to say what needs to be said in Washington, and I'm proud to have him standing with us as
we kick off this General Election," said Wes Climer. "This campaign is about the same thing it's always been about: cutting
wasteful spending, defending our constitutional rights, and making sure South Carolina's Fifth District has a voice in Congress
that actually fights for it. I'm asking folks across the district to join us in Richburg and help us build the momentum we need to
win in November."

Climer, currently a South Carolina State Senator representing District 15, is the Republican nominee for the open SC-5 seat being
vacated by Rep. Ralph Norman. He faces Democrat Mallory Dittmer in the November 3 General Election.

About US Senator John Kennedy

John Kennedy was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2016 and reelected in 2022. He has built a distinguished career as a conservative
champion for the people of Louisiana and a dedicated watchdog of taxpayer money.

During his first term in the Senate, Kennedy passed several bills to protect our stock market from foreign corruption, extend
flood insurance protection for Louisiana homeowners, stop corrupt lobbyists, and preserve disaster relief programs for small
businesses.

No other Louisiana senator has passed more bills during his or her first term.

About Wes Climer

Wes Climer is a South Carolina State Senator and the Republican nominee for South Carolina's Fifth Congressional District. He has
served in the South Carolina Senate since 2016, where he chairs the Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee.

[] [] Donate [] | Facebook [] | X / Twitter [] | Instagram TICKETS FOR THE EVENT [] Dear Peter, Join Wes Climer and Special Guest US Senator John Kennedy (R-La) for an exciting General Election Campaign Kickoff Event! When: Thursday, August 13th, 6:00 pm - 7:30 pm Where: The Gateway Conference Center | 3200 Commerce Drive, Richburg, SC General Admission $50 VIP Admission $3,500 | VIP Couple $5,000 (VIP tickets include a private reception at 5:30pm & reserved seating) [] TICKETS FOR THE EVENT [] Wes Climer, the Republican nominee for South Carolina's Fifth Congressional District, will kick off his General Election campaign next Thursday, August 13, with a rally featuring U.S. Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana. Wes Climer is running for Congress with a clear conservative vision: secure our border, cut taxes and government spending, protect parental rights, defend faith and family, restore accountability in Washington, and put America First. He's proven he'll stand up to the political establishment when it's the right thing to do, and now he's ready to take that same fight to Congress. Winning this general election is critical to ensuring South Carolina's 5th District has a proven conservative leader who will deliver results—not just make promises. Doors for General Admission ticket holders will open at 5:00 PM, with a VIP reception beginning at 5:30 PM for VIP ticket holders. General Admission tickets are $50; VIP tickets are $3,500 per person or $5,000 per couple and include a reception with hors d'oeuvres, a meet-and-greet with Wes, Senator Kennedy, and other conservative leaders. VIP ticket holders will also has assigned seating for the event. Space is limited and advance registration is required for all attendees. You can RSVP by clicking this link. [] Senator Kennedy, known for his plainspoken defense of conservative principles in Washington, will join Climer to discuss fiscal responsibility, constitutional government, and the stakes of the November election for South Carolina families. Kennedy serves on the Senate Appropriations, Banking, Budget, and Judiciary Committees. "Senator Kennedy has never been afraid to say what needs to be said in Washington, and I'm proud to have him standing with us as we kick off this General Election," said Wes Climer. "This campaign is about the same thing it's always been about: cutting wasteful spending, defending our constitutional rights, and making sure South Carolina's Fifth District has a voice in Congress that actually fights for it. I'm asking folks across the district to join us in Richburg and help us build the momentum we need to win in November." Climer, currently a South Carolina State Senator representing District 15, is the Republican nominee for the open SC-5 seat being vacated by Rep. Ralph Norman. He faces Democrat Mallory Dittmer in the November 3 General Election. About US Senator John Kennedy John Kennedy was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2016 and reelected in 2022. He has built a distinguished career as a conservative champion for the people of Louisiana and a dedicated watchdog of taxpayer money. During his first term in the Senate, Kennedy passed several bills to protect our stock market from foreign corruption, extend flood insurance protection for Louisiana homeowners, stop corrupt lobbyists, and preserve disaster relief programs for small businesses. No other Louisiana senator has passed more bills during his or her first term. About Wes Climer Wes Climer is a South Carolina State Senator and the Republican nominee for South Carolina's Fifth Congressional District. He has served in the South Carolina Senate since 2016, where he chairs the Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee. ## Michigan highlights the Left's growing radicalism...

El-Sayed is running for Senate in a historic swing state, which already makes his potential election significant.
But this comes right after the DNC elevated Michigan to its list of early states that will help decide the party's next presidential nominee.
In other words, they have just made El-Sayed and his socialist agenda a major player on the national stage.
This is a self-inflicted wound of the first order.
The Democrat Party has been shifting hard to the left for years.
And now, with the election of Democratic Socialists like Mamdani, the most radical elements of the left are becoming the new normal.
It's concerning, but if you ask me, it's also something that Republicans can take advantage of in the upcoming elections.

This AM, my finance team and I met to talk through the numbers. My MAGA opponent, Michele Tafoya, has Trump's full backing and a rolodex of dark money donors. Ahead of the primary on August 11th, she’s flooding Minnesota with MAGA lies and attacks on my record. If we wait, we risk letting Tafoya dominate the airwaves and drown out our message. So I took a risk that I hope will pay off. subject: We Have the Oil. So Why Are We Paying More?
body:
The math is simple: America has the oil, but we need the refining capacity to put America First.

| | | | | | | [VIEW THIS EMAIL IN BROWSER](https://mailchi.mp/ec110c977f0f/to-my-dad-on-fathers-day-2375658?e=3cb50a0604)

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
**Refine baby, Refine** _By Austin Sidwell
_ "They're making too much money based on a shortage..."
President Donald Trump admonished oil companies this week in the midst of the on again, off again conflictin Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. An easy target of scorn with the national average price per gallon hovering around $4.09. Public disdain is high. But the number ofoptions seems incredibly low.

The establishment in DC does a great job of pointing fingers but not offering alternatives. So let's do a little math. Where does the US stand as far as oil production, oil refinement, and do we produce enough oil to take care of our own?
The United States is the 4th largest exporter of oil in the world. We're behind Saudi Arabia, Russia and Canada, but higher than the UAE, Kuwait, Iraq and Iran. While this may be news to many people there's something even more impressive. We actually export more oil than we import. We export 10.7M barrels of oil while we import 7.9M barrels of oil. In other words, if we used our own oil and didn't import anything, we'd still have excess to sell in the world market.
A country of 89 million people who don't own, nor can they claim any sovereignty over a waterway, should not dictate affordability in our country! We have the capability of producing enough oil to take care of our own. Which begs the questions of why aren't we? Where are we deficient in the economic food chain relating to oil, refinement and transportation?
This brings us to the crux of the discussion, refineries. While the US has 132 refineries nationwide, we don't have enough. Comparatively, the bulk of refinement is done in other countries around the world. While we have supply, demand, we're not at full capacity to refine what we produce. We have elected officials in Washington who've neglected to look at the underlying issue.
Solution:refine baby refine.

We don't need a government program or to fork over tax dollars to create a pork project to drive industry leaders, we need tax incentives. We need to get out of the way of oil companies willing to invest in this country. Oil refineries employeehundreds of American workers, thousands of American workers are needed to build the facilities, and ultimately American taxpayers will pay less at the pump when we don't have to factor in transportation and shipping costs. Refineries and holding on to our own supply of oil places us in a truly unique situation which cries "America First."
When the math doesn't math, our elected officials tell us it's somebody else's problem. But the math is simple, we consume 20% of the world's oil, but we refine about 15%. We can do better. We can at least tell the world, we're a sovereign nation and we won't let anyone dictate our economy. The war with Iran is about more than oil. But while we fight against extremism, we can't let terrorists win at the pump.

Royce then went on to win two championships in Canada before moving over to play Big 3 Basketball. As the season went on, White would touch on taboo topics such as Gain of Function Research, The Federal Reserve, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden, Larry Hoover, Jeff Fort, Muammar Gaddafi, The Great Reset, Ivermectin, Me Too, etc.

Would you believe it? Donald Trump has found yet another way to cash in on the presidency. This time, he's turning his own words and presidential announcements into a product that Wall Street insiders can buy access to. Trump has launched a service called "Truth API" that will reportedly charge banks, hedge funds, and high-frequency trading firms as much as $100,000 a month for faster access to his Truth Social posts. Think about what that really means. When Trump announces a new tariff, threatens another country, praises a company, or hints at a policy change, those posts can move billions of dollars through the markets in seconds. Under this scheme, wealthy Wall Street firms that can afford a six-figure subscription get that information first — and can trade with this privileged information. And who knows? Maybe some of those same traders can just hop onto Kalshi or Polymarket to bet on markets that the president’s announcements can impact. That is corruption. Plain and simple. **I have urged that the SEC immediately investigate whether this scheme violates laws designed to prevent insider trading and market manipulation. But we also need Americans across the country to make clear that no President should be allowed to use the power of public office to enrich himself.** [**Add your name to demand an end to this corrupt pay-to-play scheme, stop the President and Wall Street executives from cashing in on public office, and protect fair markets for everyone.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-truth-api/?source=EW_EMZ32R_API_ENG_20260804_F&t=8&akid=2979%2E4032634%2E8d61gb) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-truth-api/?source=EW_EMZ32R_API_ENG_20260804_F&t=9&akid=2979%2E4032634%2E8d61gb)
---
What’s more: The stock market only works when everyone plays by the same rules.
But when wealthy Wall Street firms can pay to get the President's market-moving posts before everyone else, they're buying an advantage ordinary Americans can never have.
That's not a fair market.
It's a rigged one.
Working families already face a system tilted toward the rich and powerful. The President shouldn't be making it worse by turning the presidency into another way to make himself — and Wall Street — richer.
[**We need to speak out on this. If you support our investigation and agree that this type of corruption needs to be called out and stopped, add your name today.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-truth-api/?source=EW_EMZ32R_API_ENG_20260804_F&t=10&akid=2979%2E4032634%2E8d61gb)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

| Dear Friend,
MCPP is growing. Over the past few years, our small team in Jackson has helped make some rather large things happen. Mississippi became the first state since 1980 to legislate to abolish its income tax. School funding was rewritten so that the money follows the child, not the bureaucracy. This year, Certificate-of-Need reform passed, reducing red tape. Twice since 2021, our team has won the Bob Williams Award — including Biggest State Win in America for 2025. Not bad for a team you could seat around a single table. Our MississippiWire.News reports on what is happening across the state, and our OpenData tools are helping put data in the hands of ordinary people. See for yourself at [mspolicy.org/capabilities](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=260e22e313&e=5703353baa "https://mspolicy.org/capabilities"). Would you like to be part of the team helping change Mississippi? Now we need one more pair of hands. We are looking for a superb new executive assistant — someone to come and join our small but productive team. This person will be in charge of overseeing Development administration: the engine room that keeps our fundraising, our events, and our donor relationships running smoothly. Here is the thing — no experience is necessary. What is vital is masses of initiative. We want someone who can learn what needs doing, and then do it — consistently, and with real attention to detail. If you are the sort of person who spots the job before anyone asks, you will fit right in. Why join a small team? Because at a small organization that punches this far above its weight, nothing you do is peripheral. We are a small think tank with serious capabilities — and we are showing the other forty-nine states how it is done. If that sounds like you — or like someone you know — I would love to hear from you. Send a CV to us directly at [office@mspolicy.org](mailto:office@mspolicy.org "mailto:office@mspolicy.org"), or apply through our [LinkedIn posting](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=835a776bcc&e=5703353baa "https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4446647884/").

| | | | | | Peter,

**Today is the day. Voting in our primary election comes to a close at 8 pm tonight.**

This is our chance to bring more problem-solving, less politics back to Washington’s 5th Congressional District - _because a representative who listens to and fights for the people of this vast, beautiful district is the very least we deserve.
_
Working families, seniors, veterans, farmers, and young people in Eastern Washington have been ignored by a representative catering to extreme Party leadership and special interests, rather than addressing the challenges we face.

We deserve a representative who will listen, work hard, and answer to the people of this district.
**
It’s time for a change, and I’m ready to lead the charge as the voice that Eastern Washington deserves.**

If you have already returned your ballot, thank you for making your voice heard. If you haven’t, please remember that your ballot must be postmarked no later than 8 p.m. today, August 4, or dropped off at a designated ballot dropbox by then.

**To track your ballot, find a nearby official dropbox or voting center, or print a replacement ballot, visit**[**VoteWA.gov**](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=13ab7958e3&e=a7b299e420)**.**

**If you're a Ferry, Spokane, or Stevens County Voter and need help getting a replacement ballot, contact your County Elections or Auditor’s Office right away.**

As a proud third-generation Eastern Washingtonian, it would be the honor of a lifetime to serve you in Congress. I hope I have your vote - together we will make history.

With sincere thanks,

Carmela

body:

Thank you, Null.
The polls are open across Michigan right now, and I’m feeling so grateful.
Michiganders are bubbling in a circle next to my name today, and I genuinely appreciate each and every one.
So many hardworking folks on this grassroots team chipped in, volunteered, and stood with me because they believed in what this campaign is about – giving working Michiganders a fighter in the U.S. Senate. I’m so proud of what we’ve accomplished.
I love this state so much. Every union hall, every diner, every porch, every hug, every conversation, every parking lot at six in the morning – I've loved doing this, and I've loved doing it with all of you.
So whatever happens, please know, I appreciate you, Null. And I’ll always keep fighting for you.
| | [DONATE](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/31335?t=3&akid=3724%2E49239%2EOrsco3)

With gratitude,

Haley
P.S. Michiganders, if you haven't voted yet, polls are open until 8 p.m.
|

**A note from Haley Stevens:** Null, I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. That’s why I’ve fought so hard for working families my entire life. Now, I’m running for Michigan’s open Senate seat to continue fighting for the people and communities I love. The path to the Senate majority runs right through Michigan, which means this race is shaping up to be the most competitive and expensive in the entire country. The GOP is already coming after me as a top target for defeat, so I’m counting on your grassroots support to fight back and win. body:
Elon Musk is pulling out the same bag of tricks to keep the GOP’s grip on power in place — here’s how we’re fighting back.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260804-1&t=1&akid=3817%2E587540%2EX5Bvk6)
Peter,
I wish I could say I’m surprised by this level of corruption — but I’m not.
**Elon Musk, the newly minted, first and only trillionaire in history, is gearing up to drop millions in the midterms with one explicit goal: keep the GOP’s grip on power firmly in place.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260804_1_elon.FE-bdM&refcode=em20260804-3817&t=2&akid=3817%2E587540%2EX5Bvk6)
He’s pouring buckets of cash into reviving America PAC, the exact same apparatus that spent **$260 million** to propel Trump back into the White House.
This is everything that’s broken about politics right now. And it’s exactly why young voters are so exhausted and disillusioned with our current leaders and the system at large.
It’s why so many of them choose to stay home on Election Day — they don’t believe their voices matter. Not when corporate cash and literal trillionaires are calling all the shots.
**[Pitch in $5 right now to help our candidates fight back against Elon’s flood of cash.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260804_1_elon.FE-bdM&refcode=em20260804-3817&amount=5&t=3&akid=3817%2E587540%2EX5Bvk6)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260804_1_elon.FE-bdM&amount=5&refcode=em20260804-3817&t=4&akid=3817%2E587540%2EX5Bvk6)**
Ever since _Citizens United_ (and quite frankly, _Citizens United_ 2.0 earlier this year), there’s been virtually no limit to how the wealthy and powerful can bend the edges of our democracy to their will. And it is _always_ at the expense of working people.
But we aren’t going to sit back and take this.
At Leaders We Deserve, we’re backing a new generation of leaders who refuse corporate cash and special interest money. Leaders who can’t be bought by anyone.
_That_ is what will restore trust in our democracy and give young voters a reason to hope for the future. In the face of such blatant corruption, we can’t afford to play it safe. We’ve got to hit the pavement running full speed ahead.
Winning isn’t going to be easy. But it’s possible if we stand behind the right leaders with the right message, and make sure they have the resources they need to compete everywhere.
They have millions — at this point, _trillions_ — on their side.
**But we have something much more powerful.** _We have the people._ Supporters like you showing up to power our work, and candidates with a backbone and the moral courage it takes to meet this moment and _win_.
**[Our democracy isn’t for sale to the highest bidder. If you stand by that, please pitch in $5 now to help Leaders We Deserve continue backing audacious, forward-thinking leaders and power their path to victory in November.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260804_1_elon.FE-bdM&refcode=em20260804-3817&amount=5&t=5&akid=3817%2E587540%2EX5Bvk6)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

* * *
It's been roughly two months since anyone has actually laid eyes on Mitch McConnell. Two months of silence around the senior senator from Kentucky -- and this past week was supposed to be when that silence finally broke.
A lot of people had talked themselves into this deadline conspiracy: that any day now we'd get the announcement McConnell had died, quietly timed so there'd be no special election, no messy democratic process, nothing. The last twenty-four to forty-eight hours were supposed to be the window -- the moment we'd finally learn what the hell is going on, or the moment somebody made a move.
The answer, as far as I can tell, is nothing. Nothing is going to change. We're just going to keep drifting through this stalemate while the people who are supposed to run this country keep playing games with the disappearance of a sitting United States senator.
And I'll be honest with you: at this point, I don't even really care if Mitch McConnell is dead or alive. I don't wish the man ill. I had significant political disagreements with him -- that's well documented -- but that's not what has me angry. What has me angry is the way the whole system works. I'm angry that everything in this country is treated like a game. That it's covered like a game by the media. I'm angry at every single person who has played a role in this charade. And I keep coming back to the same conclusion: these are not partisan issues.
We cannot have a functioning government where multiple members of Congress can simply vanish and nobody seems to care. We cannot have a functioning Congress where members -- Democrats and Republicans alike -- are dying of what is essentially old age, and still expect that anything is going to get done to make our lives better.
Some of you are going to read this and think it's about ageism. It isn't -- truly. There are plenty of people out there with real wisdom and hard-won experience, and that wisdom should be shared, some of it in the halls of Congress. But when you have a Congress that is this far out of step -- politically, culturally, spiritually -- with the people it claims to represent, you get exactly what we have right now: a government that is not responsive in any meaningful way to what we actually need.
The President of the United States is an old, demented freak -- the oldest man ever elected to the office. He doesn't know what day it is, let alone how you're suffering inside the economy he helped build. The average member of Congress is sixty-eight years old. The average voter is forty-one. The average person in this country is thirty-eight. How could these people possibly understand what's happening to the rest of us?

At this point, I've talked myself all the way into it. Term limits. Age limits. Radical transparency for financial records, so we can finally root out the corruption and the outright theft of taxpayer money happening inside our own government. And radical transparency for health records, too. Because here's the truth: you give up your right to privacy the moment you go serve in the federal government. That's the penalty you pay. We cannot keep letting people head to Washington for no reason other than to get rich and famous. That has to stop.
And I know Washington is not going to suddenly wake up and solve any of this. What's happening to McConnell right now has happened to Democrats before -- I'm not going to sit here and list them all out, but we all know, deep down, that this is not a partisan problem. It's a function of a system built to protect itself.
I'm flabbergasted. I'm exhausted. And every little update chips away at my dignity and my sanity in ways I didn't see coming. It is a constant indignity to watch McConnell's staffers stroll smugly through the halls of Congress with no answers. To watch members of Congress act like they expect to see him again, when they don't know a single thing more than you or I do. To watch sitting United States senators in their sixties and seventies tell us we don't need age limits or term limits -- because they're personally planning to serve until they're eighty, ninety, a hundred, God knows how long. It's too much.
We have a government so unresponsive to our needs that it now lives in an entirely bizarre world of its own. And I'm sure plenty of people in the DC consulting class are going to read this and decide I'm being unfair to them. I don't believe I am. I think I'm speaking for how most Americans actually feel right now. People are tuning out and checking out of our democracy every single day. A lot of that is the economy, obviously -- but a lot of it is simply people feeling like their government does not represent them. That is not a left or right issue. It's not conservative or liberal. It's not the DSA versus the Nick Fuentes wing of the Republican Party. It comes down to one thing: whether people believe their government wakes up every morning trying to make their lives better.
And yeah -- it's easy to sit here and blame Donald Trump for all of it. Obviously Trump is an old, demented man and a genuinely terrible president. My record of calling him out for well over a decade speaks for itself. But this problem is so much deeper than him. Trump is a symptom. A healthy, functioning democracy -- a healthy society and culture -- never lets a man like Donald Trump ascend the way he has. It never lets an entire generation of failed political leaders cling to power this long.
So reforming our democracy has to be a must. Massive campaign finance reform. An end to gerrymandering. Reversing Citizens United. And a dozen other fights beyond those. It's going to take a lot of people making a lot of very hard decisions -- and realistically, it's the Democratic Party that's going to have to do it, because for all its imperfections, the Democratic Party is the only real force for good and change left in our system.
So we keep fighting. But man, I'll tell you -- there are days I am absolutely losing my fucking mind. And I appreciate this community more than you know. I read every comment. I read every reply that lands in my inbox. I don't always write back, but I read them, and your rage and your anger remind me that I am not alone. It keeps me in the fight. And I hope, in some small way, I'm doing the same for you.
Stay safe.
