subject: Sign: "Fire Doug Burgum for Being a National Embarrassment, an Incompetent Clown, and an Enabler of Trump's Obvious Lies"
body:
How does this guy still have a job???
| | | | |
---
| | | **[Sign:"Fire Doug Burgum for Being an Incompetent Clown, and an Enabler of Trump's Obvious Lies"](https://default.salsalabs.org/T6c1b0668-bfea-47ab-a844-a3e1ed6e6b3c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** If you’ve ever watched a Trump cabinet meeting, pointed at the TV, and shouted, _“Who the f_ ** is that guy?”* the odds are you were pointing at Doug Burgum—the former governor of North Dakota and the guy who somehow looks exactly like the stock photo that came with the $1.99 picture frame you just bought.[](https://default.salsalabs.org/T8adea4ac-83ca-43ab-9345-b56a51201615/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) He’s also managed to become one of the most embarrassingly incompetent interior secretaries in modern American history. And apparently has no problem repeating Donald Trump’s most obvious lies. Oh... and that Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool that’s now the world’s largest mixture of lime Jell-O, snot, and Vulcan blood? Burgum helped make that happen. Oh, and that Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool that is now the world’s largest trough of lime Jello, snot, and Vulcan blood? Burgum was key to making that happen: As secretary of the interior, Burgum oversees the National Park Service and was the point person for the Reflecting Pool renovation. His department:
* Awarded the rushed $14.7 million resurfacing job without competitive bidding.
* Used a contractor whose installation was later found to be flawed.
* Continued defending that contractor as having done a “fantastic job.”
* Decided to use the same company for repairs instead of seeking new bids.
* Apparently withheld or delayed records showing installation problems while the government prosecuted someone for supposed vandalism.

And now comes the truly infuriating part. Even after prosecutors led by Trump superfan Jeanine Pirrot abandoned the vandalism case because the evidence didn’t support it, Burgum is **still** repeating Trump’s false claim that vandals caused the damage. When you’re more full of shit than Jeanine Pirrot, that is one hell of an accomplishment. In short, he’s incompetent, he’s a Trump sychofant, and he apparently couldn’t give a rat’s ass about the truth. [**Add your name, and demand that Burgum be fired.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/Ta43bdca8-b6e6-4fcd-bbfb-fe121be9c705/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

I've spent most of my life around leaders – in the Navy, at NASA, and in the Senate. And I can tell you: Sherrod Brown understands what it means to be a true leader.
**He’s simply one of the toughest fighters for working families I have ever met.**
I watched Sherrod up close in the Senate. When a vote was hard, he didn't check a focus group or call a billionaire donor. He asked one question: Is this good for the people who make this country work? That kind of moral clarity is what makes Sherrod special.
Washington is a place where a lot of "leaders" sell out to the highest bidder. But Sherrod never did. Not once. Ask anyone who served with him – that record is rare.
That's exactly why we need him back in the Senate.

| | | | Hi Friend,
Polls for this year's Republican primary close at 7pm tonight.
_That's just _2 more hours_ to make your voice heard!_
2 hours left to vote for **balancing the federal budget** to leave future generations a healthy economy and a country full of opportunity
2 hours left to vote for **rooting out the fraud and wasteful spending** in the government and entitlement programs
2 hours left to vote for a **5% tax rate** for hardworking families earning under $200,000
2 hours left to vote for making the**$40,000 SALT deduction permanent**
2 hours left to vote for an **affordable and reliable energy** strategy that keeps costs low
2 hours left to vote for **unlocking the housing market** with portable mortgages and indexing capital gains to inflation
2 hours left to vote for securing **dignified career options** for all students and standing up for the sacred role of parents in their child's education
2 hours left to vote for ensuring our **veterans and their families** have access to the services they need
2 hours left to vote for steadfastly **upholding the Constitutional freedoms** of every citizen
_**2 hours left to vote for Restoring Faith in the American Dream.**_
_If you're heading home from work, stop by your polling place first,**it only takes a few minutes.**_
Find your polling place here: [www.elections.virginia.gov/casting-a-ballot/polling-place-lookup/](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
**If you've already voted, respond to this email!** I'd love to hear about your experience.
I am beyond grateful for every single person who has stood with this campaign, knocked doors, made calls, shared a post, or simply shown up to vote today. Thank you for trusting me with this fight, VA-10.
---
| | | God bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

Team,
When Dan Meuser heard about how strong our grassroots fundraising is, he said:
**[" Money won't be a problem."](https://substack.com/redirect/c2795789-a241-4a8c-b6a6-4ef9b9be808f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Of course he thinks that. Meuser has his own millions and a war chest full of corporate interest cash. He thinks he can buy himself another term in Congress. He's wrong.
**This race won 't be decided by DC insiders and billionaire donors. It'll be decided by the people in our part of PA. And the people are done with Dan Meuser.**
Meuser has never held a town hall. He kicked 30,000 of his constituents off their health care. He's doubled his net worth to over $69 million trading stocks while voting to raise costs for the rest of us.
**Money may not be a problem for Dan Meuser. But accountability will be.**
**[Chip in today to help our grassroots campaign take on Meuser 's millions and kick him out of Congress.](https://substack.com/redirect/a6af142e-da5b-463d-80f3-b40c28d452a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you,
Rachel Wallace

By now, Derek, you’ve probably heard the story. Qatar gifts our president a 250-foot, $400 million luxury jet. The president wants it to replace Air Force One. Fast-tracks some upgrades. Calls it “magnificent,” and boasts about it. **It turns out — according to _The New York Times_ — that the aircraft is lacking essential national security components, and is reportedly missing missile defense systems and the wiring to shield against an electromagnetic pulse attack.** So the Justice Department subpoenaed the phone records of the four journalists who broke that story, went after their relatives’ phone records too, and backed down only last week when a federal judge pushed back. It was one of the most blatant attacks on the free press in American history, and it will not be the last. It’s also why I immediately opened up an investigation into these abuses. **I will not let Donald Trump and his acolytes intimidate reporters into silence without exposing, at every turn, exactly what they are trying to hide from the American people.** But I can’t do it alone, especially when Republicans hold the majority in the Senate and use it to shield the president. **[Will you pitch in any amount, even $10, to help us uplift the Democrats running in this November’s elections?](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/7929?t=12&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_080426_NYT&akid=10034%2E5257348%2Em6dcAa)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | [DONATE $10→](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/7929?t=13&amount=10&express_lane=true&refcode=aschiff_email_080426_NYT&akid=10034%2E5257348%2Em6dcAa)

clean_body: | It’s an attack on press freedom unlike any in modern memory. By now, Derek, you’ve probably heard the story. Qatar gifts our president a 250-foot, $400 million luxury jet. The president wants it to replace Air Force One. Fast-tracks some upgrades. Calls it “magnificent,” and boasts about it. It turns out — according to The New York Times — that the aircraft is lacking essential national security components, and is reportedly missing missile defense systems and the wiring to shield against an electromagnetic pulse attack. So the Justice Department subpoenaed the phone records of the four journalists who broke that story, went after their relatives’ phone records too, and backed down only last week when a federal judge pushed back. It was one of the most blatant attacks on the free press in American history, and it will not be the last. It’s also why I immediately opened up an investigation into these abuses. I will not let Donald Trump and his acolytes intimidate reporters into silence without exposing, at every turn, exactly what they are trying to hide from the American people. But I can’t do it alone, especially when Republicans hold the majority in the Senate and use it to shield the president. name: Courier Newsroom
subject: Your newsfeed is being bought by the far right
body:
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1003&refcode=20260804_Meta&akid=185%2E344797%2Em6AHzq ]COURIER Newsroom

Hi Peter,

Last week, Meta signed a deal to pump Newsmax content into the AI answers
on Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp — apps used by 3.9 billion people
every month.

Not just new Newsmax stories. An archive of Newsmax content.

Newsmax is the same right-wing outlet that had to pay more than $100
million to settle defamation lawsuits with Dominion and Smartmatic after
spreading lies about the 2020 election.

The same Newsmax that scores a 20 out of 100 from NewsGuard for "severely"
violating basic journalism standards.

Oceans of far-right propaganda in the archive. And Meta just licensed it
to help answer people's questions.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1005&refcode=20260804_Meta&akid=185%2E344797%2Em6AHzq ]If you're ready to fund journalism that fights back in
those same news feeds, a contribution of any amount powers COURIER's
reporting right now.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1006&refcode=20260804_Meta&akid=185%2E344797%2Em6AHzq ]Donate

One by one, the platforms where most Americans actually get their news are
being captured by right-wing billionaires. And the "news" flooding those
feeds is being captured right along with them.

Elon Musk bought Twitter and turned it into a MAGA megaphone. In January,
a consortium including Trump ally Larry Ellison's Oracle took over
TikTok's U.S. operations — with Oracle overseeing the algorithm that
decides what 170 million Americans see.

And Mark Zuckerberg? He killed Meta's fact-checking program, then started
signing AI content deals with Fox News, The Daily Caller, the Washington
Examiner, News Corp — and last week, Newsmax.

Here's what the billionaires buying these platforms don't want you to
know: their playbook only works if there's nothing credible competing in
the feed.

That's where COURIER comes in.

While legacy outlets shrink and cut and capitulate, COURIER is one of the
only progressive media organizations in the country that's growing —
building local newsrooms in battleground states and reaching millions of
readers on the exact platforms MAGA is trying to lock down. Facebook.
Instagram. TikTok. We don't get to abandon those spaces. That's where the
fight is.

But reach like that isn't free, and trustworthy sources of news like
COURIER have never been under more pressure.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1007&refcode=20260804_Meta&akid=185%2E344797%2Em6AHzq ]Every dollar you chip in helps our newsrooms produce
and distribute the fact-based reporting that competes head-to-head with
right-wing content in the feeds where elections are won and
lost.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1008&refcode=20260804_Meta&akid=185%2E344797%2Em6AHzq ]Chip in $25 to fight back

In solidarity,
COURIER Newsroom

An empty seat for Israel during a ministerial high level meeting during a United Nations conference on a two state solution for Israel and the Palestinians, at UN headquarters on July 28, 2025, in New York City. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images.
On February 20, 2015, an official of the United Nations Population Fund sent two Israeli diplomats an email containing a confidential report about a trip two weeks earlier to Washington, D.C. by Zeid Ra'ad Al-Hussein, then the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.
"For your eyes only. Do not forward," Yahav Lichner wrote to then-Israeli Ambassador to the UN Ron Prosor and diplomat Ronny Leshno-Yaar in a message sent from Lichner's personal email account, describing the report as a "classified internal summary of Zeid's meetings in Washington."
The meetings came at a time when Israel was facing an independent commission inquiry by the UN Human Rights Council over its conduct during the 2014 military offensive against the Gaza Strip.
Left: February 2015 email from Lichner to Prosor and Leshno-Yaar sharing a confidential report on Zeid al-Hussein's trip 2015 trip to Washington. Right: Translation of Hebrew text.
The document recorded private meetings that Al-Hussein held with White House officials, senators, congressional appropriations staff, AIPAC, J Street, and human rights organizations. It also revealed a concern inside Al-Hussein's office: that congressional anger over the UN inquiry could threaten American funding for the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). Lichner added that Al-Hussein had met with members of Congress including "our friend," the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, adding that Al-Hussein was "trying to do damage control and distance himself from the report."
Leshno-Yaar responded that he intended to act on the intelligence that Lichner had provided. "Thank you Yahav. I have no choice and of course without addressing this information I must act with members of Congress to make them understand," before listing the arguments he planned to make about Al-Hussein and the Gaza commission's secretariat.
"Absolutely," Lichner replied. "You are right."
The exchange was far from a one-off: Over a two-year period between 2014 and 2015, emails show, Lichner repeatedly supplied Israeli officials with internal UN documents, private meeting accounts, pre-release material, and other political intelligence--including documentation marked as "strictly confidential"--which was later used by Israeli officials to help shape their own efforts to both proactively lobby the U.S. government and undercut UN initiatives they viewed as unfavorable to Israel.
The communications showing Lichner leaking confidential information to officials in the Israeli government come from a hacked database of emails from Prosor, Israel's permanent representative to the UN from 2011 to 2015. The emails were posted online by Distributed Denial of Secrets, a whistleblower and file-sharing website, after being obtained by Handala, a hacking group believed to be tied to Iranian intelligence.
Prosor is currently Israel's ambassador to Germany, while Lichner has served since January 2025 as director of the Washington, D.C., office of UNICEF, the United Nations children's agency. Prior to joining the UN Population Fund (UNFPA), Lichner worked at Israel's mission to the UN from 2011 to early 2014.
The emails showing leaks of classified UN information and other communications with Israeli officials came from a period when Lichner served at the UNFPA and does not indicate whether or not it has continued in his role at UNICEF. Lichner previously served as Prosor's political advisor at Israel's embassy in London and later as a senior advisor at Israel's UN mission.
The emails suggest that Prosor personally promoted Lichner's UNFPA candidacy, drawing on the assistance of then U.S. Ambassador to the UN Samantha Power to privately lobby for his appointment and later providing a glowing reference letter to the agency.
That placement appeared to pay dividends as Lichner continually fed inside information from the UN to Prosor and other Israeli diplomats, including unissued draft documents authored by then-Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon, private accounts of meetings by UN officials, and internal reports marked as confidential. Lichner also provided insight and guidance on internal UN processes and deliberations related to Israel, including informing them of scrutiny of its conduct in Gaza and the West Bank.
UN officials are subject to [rules](https://substack.com/redirect/d37a91a9-a406-41dd-b1dd-c425ceef2b6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) defining staff as international civil servants whose responsibilities are "not national but exclusively international." The organization's internal guidelines also strictly prohibit officials from communicating information to any "government, entity, person or any other source any information known to them by reason of their official position."
A former senior UN official confirmed that the behavior documented in the emails is expressly prohibited by UN guidelines.
"When you join the UN you are bound to serve the UN rather than the country you came from, and as such you are bound to promote the interests of the organization. You sign a piece of paper acknowledging that you have become a UN official and, as a result, are bound to confidentiality and serving the interests of the organization rather than a member state," Charles Petrie, a former senior UN diplomat and Assistant Secretary-General, told Drop Site News. "But there are no systems in the UN to impose consequences for leaking information. In the U.S. government, when you leak, you are actually committing a crime because you have accepted the conditions under which you are able to access different levels. That does not exist at the UN."
He added, "It is a sign of an institution that does not have internal accountability. And the higher you go, the less accountability there is."
Lichner, Prosor, and Power did not respond to detailed requests for comment. UNICEF did not respond to a request for comment.
## **Strictly Confidential**
On November 10, 2014, Lichner received an internal daily report from the UN Operations and Crisis Centre (UNOCC) providing security and political updates from various regions of the world. The report was marked, "UN STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL - NOT FOR FURTHER DISSEMINATION," citing the UN's information classification rules and with an additional note in the body further emphasizing that the report is "sensitive and the Chef de Cabinet has directed that it not be disseminated further," a reference to Ban Ki-moon's chief of staff.
Lichner forwarded the report the next morning to six Israeli diplomats with the comment, "For your eyes only," pointing to a segment on civilian casualties from U.S. operations in Iraq and opining that, "there are no statements of condemnation from the Secretary-General and no commissions of inquiry into harm to innocent people"--an evident contrast to the focus at the time on Israel's actions in Gaza by the organization.
The UNOCC report was a roundup of assessments from different conflict hotspots and classified confidential. The archive communications do not indicate whether any of its contents were useful to Israeli diplomats.
But other communications in the archive suggest the information that Lichner provided to the Israeli government was useful in their efforts to resist pressure from the international community over the 2014 war in Gaza and the ongoing occupation of the West Bank, including shaping the communications of senior UN officials to whom Lichner had privileged access.
A few months earlier, on July 4, 2014, writing from his UNFPA account, Lichner had sent five Israeli diplomats what he called "the UN internal/confidential weekly report on Jordan." The document contained accounts of closed consultations with Jordan's interior minister, border-security developments, and domestic unrest.
Five days later--one day after Israel launched Operation Protective Edge in Gaza--Lichner supplied Prosor, Deputy Ambassador David Roet, and three other mission officials with two additional documents: a letter Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas had sent Ban Ki-moon and an unpublished draft of the UN chief's reply.
The letter from Ban was still a work in progress and Lichner indicated to Israeli diplomats that he was helping shape it from the inside to be more favorable to Israel's concerns. Lichner wrote that he was working with an unnamed female "friend" privy to internal deliberations at the organization--a formulation that comes up frequently in the emails--to improve the draft "as much as possible."
"For your eyes," Lichner wrote. "I am working with our friend on improvements to the Secretary-General's letter, as much as possible." When Roet said the draft had not arrived, Lichner sent it again. "We are working to insert a reference to the rocket fire," he wrote, referring to rocket fire by Hamas and other Palestinian resistance groups into Israel.
Left: Email from Lichner to Israeli diplomats sharing an unpublished Ban-Ki Moon letter to Abbas in July 2014. Right: Translation of Hebrew text.
Lichner also sent Israeli diplomats internal accounts of Ban's meetings with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, Iraq's prime minister, and Amnesty International chief Salil Shetty. The Sisi report included a candid discussion of Gaza, Libya, the status of detained journalists, and human rights in Egypt. Lichner, sharing the reports from his personal email, requested "complete sensitivity."
Lichner also forwarded the agenda for a meeting of Ban's Senior Management Group--a high-level body made up of leaders of various UN departments and chaired by the secretary-general--which was scheduled to discuss a draft Security Council resolution on Palestine. He noted that Babatunde Osotimehin, the executive director of UNFPA, would attend the closed door meeting and promised to provide an update afterwards. "Information needs to be collected after the meeting," Lichner added. "As always, with sensitivity."
Left: Lichner forwarding the agenda from the SMG to Israeli diplomats in 2015. Right: Translation of Hebrew text.
In another 2015 email, Lichner passed an itemized list of information from what he described as "a source in the Secretary-General's circle," detailing internal developments at the UN. The email included information on attempts to promote particular individuals to posts within the organization, speculation about Ban Ki-moon's political future, and discussion of Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov--now director-general of Trump's Board of Peace overseeing Gaza--as a possible successor as head of the UN. "He is being mentioned in closed discussions in the Secretary-General's office as a possible candidate to replace Ban," Lichner wrote. "Keep an eye on him."
Left: Lichner sharing with Israeli diplomats a list of internal deliberations and intelligence from the UN provided by a source described as being close to the UN Secretary General. Right: Translation of Hebrew text.
The information that Lichner provided was deemed highly valuable by his former Israeli colleagues. In response to the note about the private discussions on senior appointments, Prosor replied: "Yahav, as usual, amazing and first-hand information."
In a separate episode, Lichner gave the Israeli mission what he described as an internal OHCHR summary of a UN General Assembly discussion concerning the then-special rapporteur for the Occupied Palestinian Territories, Indonesian diplomat Makarim Wibisono.
In a response, Israeli diplomat Nelly Shiloh noticed that the internal account inaccurately paraphrased an Israeli statement on the rapporteur's work. But she told colleagues they could not seek a correction. "For now we cannot change the situation because this is their internal report, which was not supposed to reach us," Shiloh wrote.
Information Lichner provided also appeared to be intended to help Israel blunt scrutiny over fatal shootings in the West Bank by providing Israeli diplomats advance warning about internal UN deliberations on human rights abuses, thus helping them prepare public responses.
In May 2014, Lichner used his personal Gmail account to send Prosor and three other Israeli diplomats a Haaretz [report](https://substack.com/redirect/aed89ae3-19ab-4518-a1a4-31565f4fdd5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) titled "UN Calls for Probe Into Shooting of Palestinian Youths." The article said that video taken at the scene suggested that two teenagers killed by Israeli troops, Mahmoud Odeh Salameh, 16, and Nadim Nuwara, 17, posed no threat to Israeli forces and reported that a senior UN official was demanding an "independent and transparent" investigation.
Left: Lichner sharing internal UN deliberations over the killing of two Palestinian teenagers and suggesting proactive Israeli messaging. Right: Translation of Hebrew text.
"For the past two days, I have been in contact with our friend about the issue," Lichner wrote, again referring to an unidentified female contact. He warned that the UN Department of Political Affairs, Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, and the OHCHR would meet the following day and that the shootings would probably be discussed. The high commissioner for human rights, Navi Pillay, had been urged by her Ramallah staff to write to Israel and issue a statement expressing concern about "excessive use of force," Lichner reported, adding that similar language might enter an upcoming briefing by the UN under-secretary-general for political affairs.
"At the advice of our friend," Lichner then supplied Israel with two counterarguments: that the UN was disregarding an existing Israeli military investigation by calling for an independent inquiry, and that it should not express concern about excessive force before that investigation was complete.
"I will update [you] after the meeting tomorrow," he concluded.
## **Gaza Accountability**
The communications between Lichner and Israeli diplomats at the UN mission came at a time when Tel Aviv was facing unprecedented scrutiny over the mass killing of civilians during the summer 2014 military campaign against Gaza.
In addition to forwarding details about Zeid Al-Hussein's meetings in DC related to the Gaza commission report, the archive includes several instances in which Lichner gave Israel advance or internal information about UN human rights proceedings involving Gaza. In February 2015, he forwarded an internal OHCHR planning email that disclosed when the UN commission of inquiry intended to release its report.
As usual, he added a warning emphasizing the secrecy of the information. "The information about the publication date of the report--after the elections--is sensitive and was not intended for distribution," Lichner wrote. "The information was not supposed to pass to the Office's staff and entered the summary below by mistake, and there is drama now."
Left: Lichner sharing internal information on UN inquiries on the 2014 war in Gaza. Right: Translation of Hebrew text.
The following month, Lichner supplied Prosor and Leshno-Yaar with internal correspondence between UN official James Rawley, then-Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, and Guardian reporter Harriet Sherwood. Sherwood was investigating allegations that she said had been leaked to her from within the UN showing that Israeli pressure had disrupted an internal process that recommended listing the Israel Defense Forces as an entity involved in human rights violations against children.
Rawley's response said the listing process was strictly confidential, remained ongoing, and was not subject to further comment.
Two days after The Guardian [published](https://substack.com/redirect/2a427a2d-c115-4d92-84e6-441183826cbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its report about Israeli pressure, Lichner forwarded Leshno-Yaar the correspondence between UN officials and the reporter, stating that it was for his eyes only and not to be used or quoted, while also attempting to identify Sherwood's source within the UN.
Left: Lichner forwarding UN responses to Guardian reporter and his analysis on possible sources of leak. Right: Translation of Hebrew text.
"The fact that The Guardian reporter approached these two (Rawley and June) indicates that the leak did not come from them. My bet is UNRWA/OCHA," Lichner wrote on March 19, before adding, "Internal correspondence--please do not use or quote."
## **" Intelligence officer in training"**
More than a year earlier, Prosor had mounted a private campaign to help place Lichner at UNFPA. In January 2014, following a telephone conversation with U.S. Ambassador to the UN Samantha Power, Prosor emailed her about Lichner's application for an external-relations position. He told Power that Lichner had ranked first in the interview process, adding: "Please don't mention that explicitly as we know it from internal sources."
Prosor claimed that Lichner's Israeli nationality was the only obstacle to his appointment and asked Power to speak personally with UNFPA Executive Director Babatunde Osotimehin to convey U.S. support for hiring what Prosor called the "best and most professional candidate." Osotimehin already knew Lichner and his work, Prosor wrote, but "needs support to reach the right decision."

When UNFPA requested a confidential reference the following month, Prosor described Lichner as a former political adviser and senior Israeli diplomat who had his "absolute trust." He gave Lichner the highest possible scores for reliability and teamwork and told the agency that he conducted himself with "the utmost integrity." By May 2014, Lichner was corresponding from a UNFPA address under the title External Relations Specialist.
Within weeks, he was again advising his former mission--but this time as an active inside source within the United Nations bureaucracy leaking confidential information in violation of UN regulations.
In June of that year, Lichner distributed a UN public-information department organizational chart and identified a unit responsible for Palestine, decolonization, and human rights. He suggested examining its personnel and cutting posts when the department's budget reached the General Assembly's Fifth Committee.
Left: Lichner sharing a UN organizational chart. Right: Translation of Hebrew text.
The emails suggest that Prosor remained an influential patron in Lichner's UN career as he progressed higher within the organization.
In May 2015, Lichner prepared third-person talking points for Prosor to use in promoting him for a prospective position as secretary of the UN Development Program (UNDP) Executive Board. The document instructed Prosor, who had an upcoming meeting with the director of external relations at the agency, that it was important to press a senior UNDP official on the importance of Lichner's appointment even if ultimately his hiring would be decided elsewhere.
The email itemized a list of talking points for Prosor to use to promote Lichner during the meeting. One of them states, "Yahav has very good political and analytical skills - he knows exactly what member states' political positions are," adding that he is an "intelligence officer in training and was as a political officer in the Israel embassy in the UK, working with the MPs in the House of Commons and Lords."
The available emails make no other reference to Lichner working or being trained as an intelligence officer during this period.
## **Joining UNICEF**
Lichner remained in the UN system after the correspondence documented in the archive and began working on issues more directly tied to Israeli interests at the organization. In 2016, he served as UNFPA's interim representative in Britain, and by 2019 public materials identified him as a senior UNICEF adviser. In October 2023, he joined UNICEF's executive director in a meeting with French Foreign Minister Catherine Colonna concerning civilian protection and humanitarian access in Israel's genocidal war on Gaza.
Public career listings identify him as having subsequently served as principal adviser to the UN Senior Humanitarian and Reconstruction Coordinator for Gaza. In June 2024, he wrote that he had visited Washington to discuss humanitarian operations in Gaza and the implementation of Security Council Resolution 2720, which called for increased aid to Gaza, with U.S. officials. In March 2026, George Washington University described him as having been "at the forefront" of negotiations with the U.S. government, engagement on Capitol Hill, and implementation of the resolution.
Lichner is now director of UNICEF's Washington D.C. office. There is no evidence to establish whether his conduct documented in Prosor's archive continued after 2015, nor is there evidence that UNICEF knew about the correspondence when it appointed him.
But the emails documenting his past private collaboration with the Israeli government and leaks of confidential information concern many of the same institutions and issues now within his public portfolio, including dealings with Congress and humanitarian diplomacy related to the Gaza Strip.
The archive does not connect Prosor or any other Israeli officials to his later appointment to a senior role at UNICEF.
In April 2015, however, after Lichner thanked Prosor for the "tailwind" surrounding a boost to his standing at UNFPA, Prosor offered a satisfied reply on his efforts to help Lichner ascend within the UN bureaucracy: "Glad we had an influence."

On February 20, 2015, an official of the United Nations Population Fund sent two Israeli diplomats an email containing a confidential report about a trip two weeks earlier to Washington, D.C. by Zeid Ra'ad Al-Hussein, then the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. "For your eyes only. Do not forward," Yahav Lichner wrote to then-Israeli Ambassador to the UN Ron Prosor and diplomat Ronny Leshno-Yaar in a message sent from Lichner's personal email account, describing the report as a "classified internal summary of Zeid's meetings in Washington." The meetings came at a time when Israel was facing an independent commission inquiry by the UN Human Rights Council over its conduct during the 2014 military offensive against the Gaza Strip. Left: February 2015 email from Lichner to Prosor and Leshno-Yaar sharing a confidential report on Zeid al-Hussein's trip 2015 trip to Washington. Right: Translation of Hebrew text. The document recorded private meetings that Al-Hussein held with White House officials, senators, congressional appropriations staff, AIPAC, J Street, and human rights organizations. It also revealed a concern inside Al-Hussein's office: that congressional anger over the UN inquiry could threaten American funding for the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). Lichner added that Al-Hussein had met with members of Congress including "our friend," the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, adding that Al-Hussein was "trying to do damage control and distance himself from the report." Leshno-Yaar responded that he intended to act on the intelligence that Lichner had provided. "Thank you Yahav. I have no choice and of course without addressing this information I must act with members of Congress to make them understand," before listing the arguments he planned to make about Al-Hussein and the Gaza commission's secretariat. "Absolutely," Lichner replied. "You are right." The exchange was far from a one-off: Over a two-year period between 2014 and 2015, emails show, Lichner repeatedly supplied Israeli officials with internal UN documents, private meeting accounts, pre-release material, and other political intelligence--including documentation marked as "strictly confidential"--which was later used by Israeli officials to help shape their own efforts to both proactively lobby the U.S. government and undercut UN initiatives they viewed as unfavorable to Israel. The communications showing Lichner leaking confidential information to officials in the Israeli government come from a hacked database of emails from Prosor, Israel's permanent representative to the UN from 2011 to 2015. The emails were posted online by Distributed Denial of Secrets, a whistleblower and file-sharing website, after being obtained by Handala, a hacking group believed to be tied to Iranian intelligence. Prosor is currently Israel's ambassador to Germany, while Lichner has served since January 2025 as director of the Washington, D.C., office of UNICEF, the United Nations children's agency. Prior to joining the UN Population Fund (UNFPA), Lichner worked at Israel's mission to the UN from 2011 to early 2014. The emails showing leaks of classified UN information and other communications with Israeli officials came from a period when Lichner served at the UNFPA and does not indicate whether or not it has continued in his role at UNICEF. Lichner previously served as Prosor's political advisor at Israel's embassy in London and later as a senior advisor at Israel's UN mission. The emails suggest that Prosor personally promoted Lichner's UNFPA candidacy, drawing on the assistance of then U.S. Ambassador to the UN Samantha Power to privately lobby for his appointment and later providing a glowing reference letter to the agency. That placement appeared to pay dividends as Lichner continually fed inside information from the UN to Prosor and other Israeli diplomats, including unissued draft documents authored by then-Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon, private accounts of meetings by UN officials, and internal reports marked as confidential. Lichner also provided insight and guidance on internal UN processes and deliberations related to Israel, including informing them of scrutiny of its conduct in Gaza and the West Bank. UN officials are subject to defining staff as international civil servants whose responsibilities are "not national but exclusively international." The organization's internal guidelines also strictly prohibit officials from communicating information to any "government, entity, person or any other source any information known to them by reason of their official position." A former senior UN official confirmed that the behavior documented in the emails is expressly prohibited by UN guidelines. "When you join the UN you are bound to serve the UN rather than the country you came from, and as such you are bound to promote the interests of the organization. You sign a piece of paper acknowledging that you have become a UN official and, as a result, are bound to confidentiality and serving the interests of the organization rather than a member state," Charles Petrie, a former senior UN diplomat and Assistant Secretary-General, told Drop Site News. "But there are no systems in the UN to impose consequences for leaking information. In the U.S. government, when you leak, you are actually committing a crime because you have accepted the conditions under which you are able to access different levels. That does not exist at the UN." He added, "It is a sign of an institution that does not have internal accountability. And the higher you go, the less accountability there is." Lichner, Prosor, and Power did not respond to detailed requests for comment. UNICEF did not respond to a request for comment. Strictly Confidential On November 10, 2014, Lichner received an internal daily report from the UN Operations and Crisis Centre (UNOCC) providing security and political updates from various regions of the world. The report was marked, "UN STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL - NOT FOR FURTHER DISSEMINATION," citing the UN's information classification rules and with an additional note in the body further emphasizing that the report is "sensitive and the Chef de Cabinet has directed that it not be disseminated further," a reference to Ban Ki-moon's chief of staff. Lichner forwarded the report the next morning to six Israeli diplomats with the comment, "For your eyes only," pointing to a segment on civilian casualties from U.S. operations in Iraq and opining that, "there are no statements of condemnation from the Secretary-General and no commissions of inquiry into harm to innocent people"--an evident contrast to the focus at the time on Israel's actions in Gaza by the organization. The UNOCC report was a roundup of assessments from different conflict hotspots and classified confidential. The archive communications do not indicate whether any of its contents were useful to Israeli diplomats. The document contained accounts of closed consultations with Jordan's interior minister, border-security developments, and domestic unrest. Five days later--one day after Israel launched Operation Protective Edge in Gaza--Lichner supplied Prosor, Deputy Ambassador David Roet, and three other mission officials with two additional documents: a letter Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas had sent Ban Ki-moon and an unpublished draft of the UN chief's reply. The letter from Ban was still a work in progress and Lichner indicated to Israeli diplomats that he was helping shape it from the inside to be more favorable to Israel's concerns. Lichner wrote that he was working with an unnamed female "friend" privy to internal deliberations at the organization--a formulation that comes up frequently in the emails--to improve the draft "as much as possible." "For your eyes," Lichner wrote. "I am working with our friend on improvements to the Secretary-General's letter, as much as possible." When Roet said the draft had not arrived, Lichner sent it again. "We are working to insert a reference to the rocket fire," he wrote, referring to rocket fire by Hamas and other Palestinian resistance groups into Israel. Left: Email from Lichner to Israeli diplomats sharing an unpublished Ban-Ki Moon letter to Abbas in July 2014. Right: Translation of Hebrew text. The Sisi report included a candid discussion of Gaza, Libya, the status of detained journalists, and human rights in Egypt. Lichner, sharing the reports from his personal email, requested "complete sensitivity." He noted that Babatunde Osotimehin, the executive director of UNFPA, would attend the closed door meeting and promised to provide an update afterwards. Right: Translation of Hebrew text. "He is being mentioned in closed discussions in the Secretary-General's office as a possible candidate to replace Ban," Lichner wrote. "Keep an eye on him." Left: Lichner sharing with Israeli diplomats a list of internal deliberations and intelligence from the UN provided by a source described as being close to the UN Secretary General. Right: Translation of Hebrew text. The information that Lichner provided was deemed highly valuable by his former Israeli colleagues. In response to the note about the private discussions on senior appointments, Prosor replied: "Yahav, as usual, amazing and first-hand information." In a separate episode, Lichner gave the Israeli mission what he described as an internal OHCHR summary of a UN General Assembly discussion concerning the then-special rapporteur for the Occupied Palestinian Territories, Indonesian diplomat Makarim Wibisono. In a response, Israeli diplomat Nelly Shiloh noticed that the internal account inaccurately paraphrased an Israeli statement on the rapporteur's work. Left: Lichner sharing internal UN deliberations over the killing of two Palestinian teenagers and suggesting proactive Israeli messaging. Right: Translation of Hebrew text. "For the past two days, I have been in contact with our friend about the issue," Lichner wrote, again referring to an unidentified female contact. He warned that the UN Department of Political Affairs, Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, and the OHCHR would meet the following day and that the shootings would probably be discussed. The high commissioner for human rights, Navi Pillay, had been urged by her Ramallah staff to write to Israel and issue a statement expressing concern about "excessive use of force," Lichner reported, adding that similar language might enter an upcoming briefing by the UN under-secretary-general for political affairs. "At the advice of our friend," Lichner then supplied Israel with two counterarguments: that the UN was disregarding an existing Israeli military investigation by calling for an independent inquiry, and that it should not express concern about excessive force before that investigation was complete. "I will update [you] after the meeting tomorrow," he concluded. In February 2015, he forwarded an internal OHCHR planning email that disclosed when the UN commission of inquiry intended to release its report. As usual, he added a warning emphasizing the secrecy of the information. "The information about the publication date of the report--after the elections--is sensitive and was not intended for distribution," Lichner wrote. "The information was not supposed to pass to the Office's staff and entered the summary below by mistake, and there is drama now." Left: Lichner sharing internal information on UN inquiries on the 2014 war in Gaza. Right: Translation of Hebrew text. Two days after The Guardian its report about Israeli pressure, Lichner forwarded Leshno-Yaar the correspondence between UN officials and the reporter, stating that it was for his eyes only and not to be used or quoted, while also attempting to identify Sherwood's source within the UN. Left: Lichner forwarding UN responses to Guardian reporter and his analysis on possible sources of leak. Right: Translation of Hebrew text. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. **So in the dead of winter, she and her mother crossed the border into China. And found something worse.**
**Slave traders were waiting.**
In their quest for freedom from communism, Yeonmi and her mother were sold into slavery.
For two years, she survived things most of us cannot imagine. And then, at 15, she made one last desperate move: she crossed the Gobi Desert on foot, in the dark, guided only by stars, heading toward Mongolia—and from there, finally, to South Korea.
**To freedom.**

name: Paul Barringer
subject: Why don’t the rules apply to them?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Paul Barringer for Congress
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260804 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260804]
Hey Peter,
In 2025 [https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacheverson/2025/12/24/congress-million-dollar-stock-trades-2025/] , members of Congress and their immediate families made over 13,000 trades totaling over $600 million.
I think that I can speak for all of us when I say, I’m tired of our Congress only working for themselves and forgetting about the people back home once they get their fill of power. There are major loopholes in the profession that continue to be exploited at the expense of our communities, and one of the worst is congressional stock trading.
And this is not a divided issue; regardless of political affiliation, people across the country are tired of seeing our representatives pad their stock portfolios by prioritizing the interests of corporate lobbyists and wealthy owners over their constituents.
See, if you and I were to use confidential information that we learned in our jobs to trade stocks, it’s illegal, so how come when representatives like Brad Knott [https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Net+Worth+Update%3A+Representative+Brad+Knott+Made+an+Estimated+%24295.9K+in+the+Stock+Market+Last+Month] do it, it's not?
I’m fighting to bring North Carolina values to Congress, and supporting a Congressional stock trade ban is one of the best ways to do so. If we remove the ability to exploit the system, we’ll attract representatives who serve in Congress for the right reasons.
I’ve had enough of their rules only applying to us, and not them. If you agree, could you chip in to help ensure we have the resources to keep educating voters on important issues like these? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260804] Every donation brings us closer to sending Brad Knott back to Raleigh this November and making sure that the people have a voice fighting for them in Congress.
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260804]
Talk more soon,
Paul Barringer

Should members of Congress be allowed to buy and sell individual stocks while making decisions that can move markets?
I don't think so.
While most Americans don't get access to private briefings, inside information, or advance knowledge of government actions, members of Congress do.
It’s no wonder so many people have lost faith in Washington. They look at the headlines, see politicians outperforming the market, and wonder whether the system is rigged for the powerful.
That's why I introduced legislation to ban members of Congress and their spouses from trading individual stocks while serving in office — because elected officials should be focused on serving the people who sent them to Washington, not managing investment portfolios.
But the reality is that reform only happens when enough people demand it. So today, I'm asking for your voice: Will you add your name if you agree that members of Congress should be banned from trading individual stocks while in office? [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/ban-stock-trading]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/ban-stock-trading]
Washington works best when the people have confidence that their representatives are acting in the public interest.
Let's take one step toward restoring that trust.
Thank you for speaking up.
— Marie

| Lynchburg, VA--Following his win in the Republican primary on Tuesday, August 4th, Congressman John McGuire released the following statement.
"It has been the honor of my life to serve Virginia's Fifth District, and I'm humbled to once again earn the Republican nomination. I want to thank my opponent and her supporters for their service and spirited campaign. I look forward to working alongside them and every Republican to keep the Fifth red this November.
Since taking office, my team and I have made life better, safer, and more affordable. We returned nearly $10 million to constituents, and fought to get our veterans the care they deserve. No tax on tips, no tax on overtime, and reduced taxes on social security are making a huge difference in the lives of the people of the Fifth District.
Now the choice could not be clearer. Tom Perriello is a communist who wants to hike your taxes, explode federal spending, and wage war on affordable American energy to chase a radical climate agenda that kills jobs and drives up your bills. His work for George Soros during the worst immigration crisis in the history of our nation at the Open Society Foundation beside the Biden administration cost too many lives. His ideas were wrong for the Fifth and dangerous for the country when he was in congress, and they're wrong and dangerous today. I'll keep fighting for lower costs, a secure border, secure elections, the Second Amendment, and the freedom to worship, and to keep the Fifth the best place to live, work, and raise your family in peace. Thank you to my Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, my wife Tracy, President Trump, Speaker Mike Johnson, Former Governor Glenn Youngkin, many state delegates and senators, numerous sheriffs in and around the district, my incredible team, the rest of the congressional Republicans who helped, and everyone in the Fifth District who placed their trust in me. I am full of energy, and we are just getting started. God bless you, and God bless America."

clean_body: | | | | == == | | Lynchburg, VA--Following his win in the Republican primary on Tuesday, August 4th, Congressman John McGuire released the following statement. "It has been the honor of my life to serve Virginia's Fifth District, and I'm humbled to once again earn the Republican nomination. I want to thank my opponent and her supporters for their service and spirited campaign. I look forward to working alongside them and every Republican to keep the Fifth red this November. Since taking office, my team and I have made life better, safer, and more affordable. We returned nearly $10 million to constituents, and fought to get our veterans the care they deserve. No tax on tips, no tax on overtime, and reduced taxes on social security are making a huge difference in the lives of the people of the Fifth District. Now the choice could not be clearer. Tom Perriello is a communist who wants to hike your taxes, explode federal spending, and wage war on affordable American energy to chase a radical climate agenda that kills jobs and drives up your bills. His work for George Soros during the worst immigration crisis in the history of our nation at the Open Society Foundation beside the Biden administration cost too many lives. His ideas were wrong for the Fifth and dangerous for the country when he was in congress, and they're wrong and dangerous today. I'll keep fighting for lower costs, a secure border, secure elections, the Second Amendment, and the freedom to worship, and to keep the Fifth the best place to live, work, and raise your family in peace. Thank you to my Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, my wife Tracy, President Trump, Speaker Mike Johnson, Former Governor Glenn Youngkin, many state delegates and senators, numerous sheriffs in and around the district, my incredible team, the rest of the congressional Republicans who helped, and everyone in the Fifth District who placed their trust in me. I am full of energy, and we are just getting started. God bless you, and God bless America." _**by David Shuster**_
There is a troubling spectacle unfolding on portions of the American left. Organizations such as the Democratic Socialists of America, along with a growing chorus of progressive commentators and activists, now argue that the United States should curtail - or abandon altogether, military support for Ukraine. These left-wing commentators have framed their arguments as anti-war. But their case is weak, absurd, and impossible to reconcile with the values progressives have long claimed.
For decades, progressives have spoken about solidarity with vulnerable people, resistance to authoritarianism, defense of democracy, and opposition to colonial domination.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/35d17a6d-a5ef-4fab-8776-b09414d5a501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ukraine is a democratic state that was invaded by an autocratic Russian neighbor determined to extinguish Ukraine's sovereignty, erase its national borders, and place the Ukrainian people under the subjugation of the Vladimir Putin's Kremlin. If progressives can't support the Ukrainian cause, then progressive principles are merely shallow slogans on a web site or YouTube channel fundraising page.
Let's start with the basics. The Russia-Ukraine war is not the U.S. war in Iraq.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/35d17a6d-a5ef-4fab-8776-b09414d5a501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is not another neo-conservative adventure in regime change, nation building, or preventive invasion. Ukraine has not asked Americans to fight its battles. It has asked for Americans to fight its war. It asked for weapons, intelligence, and economic support so that Ukrainians could defend their own homes, families, and democracy. There is a great irony in hearing people who routinely condemn colonial conquest shriek and recoil at the prospect of assisting a nation resisting such a conquest.
Some of my own colleagues on the left have argued that military aid "prolongs the conflict." But this argument overlooks a basic reality: wars do not end simply because the victim stops resisting. If Ukraine lacked the means to defend itself, the outcome would not be peace. It would be brutal conquest.
The history of Russia's occupation of Ukrainian territory, starting with the Crimea invasion and annexation in 2014, includes documented abuses against civilians. In Crimea as well as the eastern Donbas region of Ukraine, there have been countless reports of Russian troops carrying out rape, torture, and murder.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/35d17a6d-a5ef-4fab-8776-b09414d5a501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There is no reason to believe that Ukraine's surrender to occupying Russian forces would produce a just or lasting peace...

A recent viral social media post by activist Amy Mekelburg ("Amy Mek") targets Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed for his inflammatory rhetoric and loaded terminology.
The post references a 2022 speech El-Sayed gave at a Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) banquet in Oklahoma, first reported by the 'Washington Free Beacon' in January 2026. According to that report, El-Sayed told attendees, "You cannot understand a ban on Sharia without understanding the Trail of Tears," and claimed the "same exact forces" behind an Oklahoma ballot measure to ban Islamic law from courts were behind the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing. El-Sayed's financial disclosures indicate he received at least $5,000 for a CAIR-Oklahoma speech.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a2458a4-62c1-45c7-892b-bc5e80c4cd1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
While Texas and Florida state governments did designate CAIR as a foreign terrorist organization in 2025, the federal U.S. government does not--and has explicitly rejected that designation. The State Department, under then-Secretary John Kerry, stated in 2014: "The U.S. government clearly does not consider CAIR to be a terrorist organization."
El-Sayed is a Democratic candidate for Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat in 2026, with degrees from the University of Michigan, Oxford, and Columbia. He has publicly associated with Muslim and progressive organizations, including serving as vice president of his university's Muslim Students Association. His remarks comparing anti-Sharia efforts to historical injustices have drawn criticism from conservative media.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1520cacc-d503-4bf7-888f-074906bcf69a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

If only the Cherokee, Choctaw, and Creek had CAIR | | | Aug 4 | | | | | | | | | | | | A recent viral social media post by activist Amy Mekelburg ("Amy Mek") targets Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed for his inflammatory rhetoric and loaded terminology. The post references a 2022 speech El-Sayed gave at a Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) banquet in Oklahoma, first reported by the 'Washington Free Beacon' in January 2026. According to that report, El-Sayed told attendees, "You cannot understand a ban on Sharia without understanding the Trail of Tears," and claimed the "same exact forces" behind an Oklahoma ballot measure to ban Islamic law from courts were behind the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing. El-Sayed's financial disclosures indicate he received at least $5,000 for a CAIR-Oklahoma speech. | | ---|---|--- While Texas and Florida state governments did designate CAIR as a foreign terrorist organization in 2025, the federal U.S. government does not--and has explicitly rejected that designation. The State Department, under then-Secretary John Kerry, stated in 2014: "The U.S. government clearly does not consider CAIR to be a terrorist organization." El-Sayed is a Democratic candidate for Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat in 2026, with degrees from the University of Michigan, Oxford, and Columbia. He has publicly associated with Muslim and progressive organizations, including serving as vice president of his university's Muslim Students Association. His remarks comparing anti-Sharia efforts to historical injustices have drawn criticism from conservative media. | | ---|---|--- . # [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8120%2E582294%2EvYhzsJ)
This is not the email I wanted to send.
We’ve been telling you that New Hampshire is a top target for national Republicans. They’re pouring millions of dollars into our state to flood the airwaves and flip this seat red.
Now new polls have our opponent just one point away from us — in the margin of error. A virtual tie.

That made him the largest individual political donor in a single election cycle in American history. **Now, Axios reports that Musk has revived America PAC for the midterms.** The group is preparing a massive operation of door-knocking, digital advertising, and direct mail to turn out Republican voters in races like Pat’s and protect the GOP majority. body:

---
Peter — I recently traveled to Pensacola to stand with Escambia County residents fighting a proposed hyperscale data center in their community. What they’re facing should concern every Floridian, because other communities across our state could be next. Here are 3 things you need to know about hyperscale data centers: | **1\. Your electric bill only moves in one direction:_up._** These facilities use staggering amounts of power, and the cost gets passed straight to you. Meanwhile, the giant utilities that seem to hold a lock on policy in Tallahassee keep posting record profits.
---
**2\. Our water is on the line.** Florida is nothing without our clean water, our beaches, our springs, and our Everglades system. Hyperscale data centers demand massive amounts of water, and families cannot afford to gamble with what makes this state livable.
---
**3\. Lawmakers cynically gave local communities room to fight back while rolling out the red carpet for the data center industry.** Local governments now have the authority to reject harmful projects — but only when residents organize, speak out, and demand action. Meanwhile, the industry got an easier path to build these massive facilities across Florida. That is not real protection, and Florida families deserve better.
---
I am running for Attorney General to stand up to the corporations and billionaires pushing these projects through, and to make sure every Florida community has the power to protect its people.
**[But taking on utility giants and big corporations with deep pockets is not easy, and I cannot do it alone. This moment wasn’t about me. It was about the work we are all doing together — the young progressives we’re electing to office to fight for what matters most.
I talked about our work electing Zohran Mamdani and Claire Valdez in NYC. This didn’t happen because it was inevitable. It happened because we showed up, did the work, and proved that a different kind of politics is possible if we demand it.

The political establishment keeps running the same failed playbook — handing complete control to the GOP and letting a corrupt, reckless Trump administration push us toward authoritarianism.
If politicians want to know how to get elected, it is not complicated. Do your job and represent the people, not the special interests buying out our elections. That’s the kind of leadership that inspires people of all ages to vote in record numbers.
That’s why the work we’re doing is so important. And we’re doing it _without_ corporate cash or shady special interests. This is a genuine grassroots effort.

| | | Fellow Patriot, The Republican National Committee's research team just uncovered another bizarre and concerning twist in James Talarico's seeming perversion of Christianity... Hey friends,
I want to tell you why Texas's 23rd Congressional District matters so much to me.
It's the district next door to the community I call home, and I've spent years traveling through it, meeting people, and listening to what matters most to them.
I care deeply about this district and it’s important to me who represents it in Congress. That’s why I'm proud to support Katy Padilla Stout.
Katy is a mom of four, a former public school teacher, and a family attorney who has spent her life standing up for children and helping families.
And she is running in one of the most important congressional races in the country against Brandon Herrera, a far-right YouTuber who calls himself the “AK Guy” and has built his career around guns, cruelty, and attention-seeking behavior.
This district has already been through one embarrassing representative. Tony Gonzales abandoned his constituents and resigned in disgrace.
Now Republicans are asking the people of TX-23 to replace him with someone who has mocked veteran suicide, made disparaging comments about women, and glorified gun violence for an online audience.
The families and communities of TX-23 deserve someone who will fight for their children, their schools, their safety, and their future. They do not deserve another representative who turns public service into a spectacle.
Katy knows these communities. She understands what families are facing. And she has the experience, compassion, and determination to represent this district with the seriousness it deserves.
But right now, Katy is being outraised. She needs to close the gap.

Fellow Patriot,

**I'll make this quick:** we have seven days until the primary, and _I need an additional 771 donations before then to prove this campaign has what it takes_.

This is a crowded field, and it may well come down to a runoff before this is settled. That just means the fight continues a little longer, and I intend to be standing strong through it all.

**My opponents have had years to build up their campaigns._I have not_.** What I do have is almost thirty years of working for the people of South Carolina, the values Lindsey and I were both raised on, and people like you who stood with him.

_Every donation between now and next Tuesday matters now more than ever_. It helps us compete and it shows South Carolina that this campaign has real support behind it heading into the primary.

**[Can I count on your support before my primary next week? Peter,

At almost every campaign stop I do across the Central Valley, I ask people the same question: **do you or someone you know drive to Tijuana to get medicine or fix your teeth?**

Almost every single time, hands go up.

I'll never get used to that. In the wealthiest country in the world, so many of my neighbors are forced to seek health care from the country my own parents left behind.

I first started asking that question at a forum in Stratford, an unincorporated community about 40 miles south of Fresno where the poverty rate exceeds 30%. But even though the border is more than six hours away, they're forced to make the drive anyway because it's still cheaper, and faster, than getting care here.

That's a policy failure — plain and simple. And it's exactly why Medicare for All is a driving force of this campaign.

clean_body: The Next Endorsement I Need Is Yours The Next Endorsement I Need Is Yours | | | | Dear America First Patriot, I'm deeply honored by his confidence, because President Trump knows Minnesota needs a Governor who will fight ALONGSIDE him--not against him. He knows our state has been devastated by failed leadership, rampant fraud, rising crime, and career politicians who talk a lot but never seem to fix anything. President Trump and I believe it's time for something different. I'm not a career politician. I'm a businessman who built one of America's most successful companies right here in Minnesota and created thousands of good-paying jobs. I've spent my life solving problems, not creating them. Meanwhile, Minnesota politicians like Amy Klobuchar and Lisa DeMuth stood by while our state suffered through one of the largest fraud scandals in American history. Families paid the price while the political establishment looked the other way. Enough is enough. As Governor, I'll work alongside President Trump to: End government fraud and corruption. Restore law and order. Work with ICE instead of standing in its way. Put America First values back in the Governor's Office. President Trump has already endorsed me. # Well, would you look at that. The last full week.

Peter,Well, here we are. The last full week before the August 11 primary, and I honestly do not know where the time went.
It feels like about ten minutes ago I was standing out at the corner of Highways 64 and 65 in downtown New Richmond, alone at rush hour on a cold February day last year, holding a homemade sign.
I was out there because I could not stomach what this administration was doing, the illegal executive orders piling up by the day and Elon Musk taking a sledgehammer to the federal services working families count on.
I stood there wondering if a single soul driving by felt the same way I did.
**Turns out a whole lot of you did.** Before I say anything else, I want to say thank you. Every one of you who signed a nomination paper, showed up to an event, knocked a door, tossed a few bucks in the pot, or just told a neighbor about this campaign, you are the reason I made it to this week at all. I mean that. This was never my campaign. It has always been ours.We are not coasting to the finish either. Here is where you can find me these last few days:**Wednesday, August 5, "Bad Faith" Screening, Ashland.** 3 pm to 5 pm at the Vaughn Public Library. A documentary on the rise of Christian Nationalism and the machinery working to tear our democracy down. Heavy stuff, and worth seeing clearly.**Wednesday, August 5, Central Park Clean Up and Potluck, Superior**. 5 to 7 pm with the Douglas County Dems. Come do a little good and eat a little good.

Come talk with me about whatever is on your mind.**Friday, August 7, Wisconsin Valley Fair, Wausau.** 3 to 7 pm at the Marathon County Dems booth. Fair food and good company, hard to beat.**Saturday, August 8, "Heart of the North" Picnic, Ojibwa.** 12 to 5 pm at Ojibwa Park, hosted by the Democratic Party of Sawyer County and the Lac Courte Oreilles Reservation. Come meet the candidates on the ballot and enjoy an afternoon in the North Woods.**Tuesday, August 11, Primary Night Watch Party, New Richmond.** This is the big one. Email [hello@armstrongforwisconsin.com](mailto:hello@armstrongforwisconsin.com) if you need details.I would love nothing more than to stand shoulder to shoulder with you Tuesday night and see what we built together.

Yesterday I introduced legislation that uses the government's purchasing power to build a real market for carbon removal technology. Carbon emissions fueled this crisis, and my constituents feel the impacts constantly, from drought to wildfire to rising seas. Removing legacy carbon from the atmosphere is not optional if we are serious.
Last week I relaunched the National Coordination on Adaptation and Resilience for Security Act with Republican Rep. María Salazar, Senator Coons, and Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski. It puts a Chief Resilience Officer in the White House so the federal government stops responding to hurricanes, floods, wildfires, and heat waves with a dozen agencies working past each other.

# **Federal appeals court upholds Florida 's ban on children attending sexually explicit drag shows**

* **The ruling vacated a lower court 's statewide preliminary injunction** that had blocked the law since 2023, finding the restaurant chain that challenged it was unlikely to succeed on its constitutional claims.

* **The law, signed by Gov. Ron DeSantis in 2023, makes it a misdemeanor to admit children to adult live performances** with sexually explicit content. Central Florida restaurant chain Hamburger Mary's had sued arguing the law was unconstitutionally vague and would chill protected speech beyond obscene performances. * **Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier called the ruling a "huge victory"** after three years of litigation. Hamburger Mary's could seek Supreme Court review.

When I filled out my ballot, I paused to reflect on everything that's made this campaign what it is.

I've talked with parents trying to make ends meet, seniors who are worried about protecting Medicare and Social Security, veterans, teachers, health care workers, small business owners, and so many others who just want a government that listens, delivers, and puts people ahead of politics...or their own interests.

_Every single conversation has stuck with me._ They reminded me of some of the conversations I had at the doors in 2018, when I decided to run for Congress in the first place. In that election, we flipped this seat blue for the first time, saw record turnout, put a big check on Donald Trump, and got to work on things like $35 insulin and a big infrastructure package to rebuild the nation and invest in clean energy. Now, in his second term, we're seeing Trump unrestrained. That is one reason the outcome of this election is so critical.

Every decision I make is about the people I have the privilege of representing—not special interests or partisan politics. Who you send to Congress matters. And what we're focused on is standing up for the people I represent and shaping the future we all want for us and our children.

**This campaign wouldn't exist without good people like you, and I am beyond grateful for your support.** My work in Congress has always been powered by people like you who believe we can solve problems, protect our fundamental freedoms, and build a future that's brighter for the next generation.

[**If you haven't already, chip in anything you can to help our campaign power through these final hours and continue reaching voters while there's still time to make a difference.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136634347/638078274/-2042773732?refcode=em26_260804_gotv4_fnd_gq_act___KS_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260804_gotv4_fnd_gq_act___KS_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=9c57d4d2-5690-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YzU3ZDRkMi01NjkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=O96oXSoXAUp_1FuUZFR8sgG0vHgrSFe5kYqXFI53dJQ=)

Thank you for believing in me, for standing with this campaign, and for everything you've done to help us get to today.

Now let's finish this together,

Kim
